final answer
The mechanism rests on the `update_stock` flag and the `dn_detail` link. I read the Delivery Note and Sales Invoice GL code in full. I didn't open the Sales Order submit code or the base GL composer, so those parts are inferred from method names and a file listing. ## Lifecycle **1. Sales Order** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`, class `SalesOrder(SellingController)`) - `on_submit` (line 450) books no stock or GL entries. It only reserves stock and updates the status. - `update_prevdoc_status` (line 435) updates linked documents. - `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py` holds the mappers: - `make_delivery_note` (line 232) creates the Delivery Note and copies the SO row reference into `so_detail`. - `make_sales_invoice` (line 425) creates the Sales Invoice. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, class `DeliveryNote(SellingController)`) - `on_submit` (line 481) calls `update_stock_ledger` in `SellingController` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`, line 676), which writes the Stock Ledger Entries. - It then calls `make_gl_entries` in `StockController` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, line 178). - `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries` (line 433) delegates to `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` (`stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`). That class extends `BaseStockGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`) and posts the standard entries: Dr COGS (or the Stock Delivered But Not Billed account) and Cr Stock In Hand. - The billing side lives in `DeliveryNote.update_billing_status` (line 645) and `services/billing_status.py`. The helper `update_billed_amount_based_on_so` (line 58) handles invoices that were made from the SO rather than the DN. - `mapper.py::make_sales_invoice` (line 62) creates the invoice from the DN and sets `dn_detail` and `delivery_note` on each invoice row. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`) - `on_submit` (around lines 436–465) runs these steps: - `update_prevdoc_status` updates the Sales Order. - `update_billing_status_in_dn` (line 1084) updates the Delivery Note's billed amount and `per_billed`. - `update_stock_ledger` runs only `if self.update_stock == 1`. - `make_gl_entries` (line 1030) builds the entries through `get_gl_entries`, which delegates to `SalesInvoiceGLComposer`. - `SalesInvoiceGLComposer` is in `accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`. Its `compose` method builds these rows: - Customer: `make_customer_gl_entry` - Taxes: `make_tax_gl_entries` - Income: `make_item_gl_entries` and `_append_item_income_gl_entry` - Plus POS, write-off and rounding rows. ## Why COGS is booked only once 1. **`update_stock` gates the invoice's stock postings.** - In `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.make_item_gl_entries` (line 374), the stock and COGS entries from `super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()` are added only `if cint(doc.update_stock)` and perpetual inventory is on. - An invoice made from a Delivery Note has `update_stock = 0`. It therefore creates no Stock Ledger Entries and no COGS entries. - The `update_stock` check in `sales_invoice.py` (line 1191) also supports this. It is not a guarantee: validation at line 1001 and the `dn_required` check at line 861 only stop you combining the two choices wrongly. - If you invoice directly with `update_stock = 1`, the invoice books the COGS itself, because no Delivery Note exists. 2. **Stock Delivered But Not Billed (SDBNB) reclassification.** - If the company has `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` set, `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account` (line 438) sets the Delivery Note's expense account to the SDBNB account. The Delivery Note then books Dr SDBNB and Cr Stock. - When the invoice is submitted, `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` (line 164) reclassifies that amount. It returns early if `update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. - For each row, `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` finds the Delivery Note row through `dn_detail`. It reads that row's `expense_account`, and `_is_sdbnb_reversal` checks that the account is of type "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" and differs from the item's expense account. - It then reads the original Stock Ledger Entry (`voucher_no` = Delivery Note, `voucher_detail_no` = `dn_detail`). From that it takes the valuation rate (`stock_value_difference / actual_qty`) and multiplies it by `item.stock_qty`. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` posts Cr SDBNB and Dr COGS (`item.expense_account`) for that amount. - The result is one expense booking, moved from the holding account to COGS at invoice time. The valuation comes from the Delivery Note's own Stock Ledger Entry, so it is not recomputed. 3. **Linking and validation.** - The `dn_detail`, `so_detail`, `delivery_note` and `sales_order` fields trace each invoice row back to its Delivery Note row and Sales Order row. - `validate_delivery_note` (around line 1025) throws if the linked Delivery Note isn't submitted. - `update_billing_status_in_dn` and `DeliveryNote.update_billing_status` update billed quantities and amounts. This stops the same delivery being billed twice and keeps `per_billed` correct. 4. **Cancellation and returns.** - Cancelling either document calls `make_reverse_gl_entries` from `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`. Each document reverses only the entries it posted. - The branch at line 1067 reverses the invoice's stock GL entries on cancel only when `update_stock` is set.

final answer
ERPNext books COGS once because only one of the two documents ever writes stock. The Delivery Note owns stock movement and COGS. The Sales Invoice, when it is billed from a Delivery Note, posts only revenue, and the `update_stock` flag plus a validation rule enforce that. Nothing I read ties the Sales Invoice's COGS entries to the Delivery Note's, so the guarantee is that two stock postings can't exist for one delivery. This version of the code is refactored, so most GL logic is in `services/` composer classes. I read all of this in the code and did not run it. ## 1. Sales Order (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/`) - The Sales Order posts no stock or GL entries. It only holds the commitment: `per_delivered`, `per_billed` and `delivered_qty` on each item. - `SalesOrder.validate` and the status services (`services/status.py`) keep those percentages and the status current. - `mapper.py` has `make_delivery_note` and `make_sales_invoice`. Both copy the Sales Order row id into `so_detail` and set `against_sales_order` or `sales_order`. - That row id is how later documents write back to the Sales Order. `SalesOrder.update_prevdoc_status` and `status_updater` handle the write-back. ## 2. Delivery Note (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`) `DeliveryNote.on_submit` runs these steps in order: - `update_prevdoc_status` raises `delivered_qty` on the Sales Order row, matched through `so_detail`. - `update_billing_status` hands off to `BillingStatusService` in `services/billing_status.py`. - `update_stock_ledger` comes from `SellingController` in `controllers/selling_controller.py`. It builds the outgoing entries from `get_item_list` through `get_sle_for_source_warehouse`, then calls `StockController.make_sl_entries`. - `make_gl_entries` calls `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries`, which uses `DeliveryNoteGLComposer`. That class extends `BaseStockGLComposer` in `erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle` follows. How the entries are built: - `BaseStockGLComposer.compose` reads each Stock Ledger Entry's `stock_value_difference`. It posts Dr the item's `expense_account` and Cr the warehouse inventory account. - That is the COGS booking, and it happens only when perpetual inventory is on. - `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account` changes the account. If "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB) is enabled on the Company, it sets `item.expense_account` to the SDBNB account instead of COGS. Delivery then parks the cost on a balance-sheet account. - It also refuses SDBNB for items linked to a Sales Invoice (`against_sales_invoice`). - `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` sets `enforce_pl_expense_account = False` so that balance-sheet account is allowed. ## 3. Sales Invoice (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/`) `mapper.py` and `delivery_note/mapper.py::make_sales_invoice` create the invoice from the Delivery Note. They copy the Delivery Note Item name into `dn_detail` and the Delivery Note name into `delivery_note`. `SalesInvoice.on_submit` does the following: - `update_billing_status_in_dn` re-sums `billed_amt` on the Delivery Note Item by `dn_detail`. It then calls `DeliveryNote.update_billing_percentage`. - `update_prevdoc_status` updates the Sales Order's billed amount. - `update_stock_ledger` runs only `if self.update_stock == 1`. - `make_gl_entries` calls `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose` in `services/gl_composer.py`. ## How COGS is booked once 1. **A Sales Invoice made from a Delivery Note has `update_stock = 0`.** - Without the flag, `SalesInvoice.on_submit` skips `update_stock_ledger`, so there is no second Stock Ledger Entry. - `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.make_item_gl_entries` calls `BaseStockGLComposer` (`super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`) only when `cint(doc.update_stock)` and perpetual inventory are both true. - With the flag off, the invoice posts customer, tax and income entries and no inventory or COGS entries. 2. **A validation blocks the double posting.** - `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note` throws "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes" if `update_stock` is set while any row has `delivery_note`. - `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` stops the same Delivery Note row from being over-billed. - `check_prev_docstatus` requires the Delivery Note to be submitted. 3. **With the SDBNB setting on, the invoice closes out the delivery's holding entry.** - The Delivery Note posted Dr SDBNB, Cr Inventory. - `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` returns early if `update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. - Otherwise, for each row with `delivery_note` or `dn_detail`, it runs `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item`. That helper looks up the Delivery Note's Stock Ledger Entry through `voucher_no` and `voucher_detail_no = dn_detail`, and takes the delivery-time valuation rate (`stock_value_difference / actual_qty`) times `item.stock_qty`. - `_is_sdbnb_reversal` confirms the Delivery Note used a "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" account that differs from the invoice's `expense_account`. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` then posts Cr SDBNB and Dr the real COGS account. - So the cost moves from the holding account to the P&L account when the invoice is submitted, and the amount comes from the original Delivery Note ledger entry, not a fresh valuation. 4. **Without SDBNB, COGS is booked at delivery time.** The Delivery Note posts Dr COGS and Cr Inventory, and the invoice adds revenue only. 5. **Direct invoicing is a separate path.** When the invoice is made straight from the Sales Order with `update_stock = 1`, the invoice does its own stock movement and COGS through the same `BaseStockGLComposer`, and no Delivery Note exists. 6. **Repost keeps the two documents consistent.** `repost_item_valuation._update_post_delivery_billed_vouchers` adds the Sales Invoices that were billed from a Delivery Note when that Delivery Note is reposted. This lets the SDBNB reversal entries match the revised Delivery Note valuation. Cancelling follows the same split. `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` calls `check_next_docstatus` and reverses the stock and GL entries, while a cancelled invoice only reverses its own entries.

final answer
ERPNext books COGS once because only one of the two documents ever posts the stock movement. The Delivery Note posts it, and the Sales Invoice is blocked from doing it again. I did not read the Sales Order code or `BaseStockGLComposer`, so those parts of this trace come from the graph and from names I saw in other files. **1. Sales Order** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`) - It posts no stock ledger entries and no GL entries. It only reserves stock and tracks progress. - Its items carry `so_detail`, which the downstream documents point back to. - When a Delivery Note or Sales Invoice is submitted, `update_prevdoc_status()` (the status updater) refreshes `delivered_qty` and `billed_amt` on the Sales Order items. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, class `DeliveryNote(SellingController)`) - `on_submit()` calls these in order: - `update_prevdoc_status()` - `update_billing_status()` - `update_stock_reservation_entries()` - `update_stock_ledger()` - `make_gl_entries()` - `repost_future_sle_and_gle()` - `update_stock_ledger()` is in `SellingController` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`). It builds the Stock Ledger Entries with `get_sle_for_source_warehouse` and `get_sle_for_target_warehouse`. `set_incoming_rate()` supplies the valuation (cost) rate for each item. - `make_gl_entries()` is in `StockController` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, line 178). It runs only when perpetual inventory is enabled and the document has stock items. It then calls `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries()`, which hands off to `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`). That class extends `BaseStockGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`). - The composer credits the inventory (stock) account and debits the item's `expense_account`. This is the COGS posting. - `validate_expense_account()` can point that expense account at the "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" account (`stock_delivered_but_not_billed` on the Company) when `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` is set. In that case the Delivery Note books the cost into an interim account instead of straight into COGS. - `on_cancel()` reverses all of this. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, class `SalesInvoice`) - A Sales Invoice made from a Delivery Note has `update_stock = 0`. Its `on_submit()` runs `update_prevdoc_status()` and `update_billing_status_in_dn()`. The second call updates `billed_amt` and `per_billed` on the Delivery Note through `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/billing_status.py`). It also marks the matching Sales Order items as billed. - `make_gl_entries()` then calls `SalesInvoice.get_gl_entries()`, which calls `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`). - That composer writes the receivable, tax and income entries. In `make_item_gl_entries`, the stock and COGS part is gated by this line: `if cint(doc.update_stock) and erpnext.is_perpetual_inventory_enabled(doc.company): gl_entries += super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()` - So when the invoice is linked to a Delivery Note and `update_stock = 0`, it posts revenue and receivable only. It adds no inventory or COGS entries and no Stock Ledger Entries, because `update_stock_ledger()` in `on_submit` is also gated on `update_stock == 1`. **Why COGS is booked exactly once** - **Stock movement:** a document posts stock and COGS only if it moves stock. For a Delivery Note that is always true. For a Sales Invoice it is true only when `update_stock = 1`. That setting is meant for direct invoicing with no Delivery Note. - **Hard guard:** `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note()` throws "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes" if `update_stock` is on and any item has a `delivery_note`. A Sales Invoice therefore cannot post stock for items already delivered. The same applies to Sales Order links through `so_dn_required()`. - **Link fields:** the `dn_detail` and `so_detail` fields tie each invoice row to its delivery row. `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing` (`erpnext/accounts/services/billing_validation.py`) stops the same delivery from being billed more than once. - **Timing gap:** if the Delivery Note is submitted well before the invoice, COGS is already in the books from the Delivery Note's submit date. The invoice later adds only revenue and receivable. With Stock Delivered But Not Billed enabled, the interim account holds the cost until billing. I did not trace how that interim account is cleared. - **Cancellation:** reversing either document uses `make_reverse_gl_entries` (`erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`). Each document reverses only the entries it posted itself.

final answer
COGS is booked once because only one of the two documents posts stock. A Delivery Note always does. A Sales Invoice only does if its `update_stock` flag is on. When an invoice is built from a Delivery Note, that flag stays 0. I traced this through the code but didn't run it or read the tests. ## 1. Sales Order - `SalesOrder` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`) posts no stock ledger entries and no general ledger entries. On submit it reserves stock and moves stock in the Bin. - It is also the parent of the later documents: - `make_delivery_note` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py` builds the Delivery Note. `sales_order.js` calls it through `frappe.model.open_mapped_doc`. - `make_sales_invoice` in the same file builds a Sales Invoice straight from the order. Its `update_item` sets the quantity to the ordered quantity minus what is already billed. - Each created row keeps a back-link to the order. Delivery Note Item carries `so_detail` and `against_sales_order`. Sales Invoice Item carries `so_detail` and `sales_order`. ## 2. Delivery Note: where COGS is booked - In `DeliveryNote.on_submit` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:481`), the call order is: - `update_prevdoc_status()`, which uses the `StatusUpdater` machinery in `erpnext/controllers/status_updater.py` to update delivered quantity and `per_delivered` on the Sales Order. - `update_billing_status()`. - `update_stock_ledger()`, defined in `SellingController` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:676`). It writes the Stock Ledger Entries. - `make_gl_entries()` then `repost_future_sle_and_gle()`. - `StockController.get_gl_entries` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:224`) builds the general ledger entries. `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` and `BaseStockGLComposer.compose` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`) read the Stock Ledger Entries. - They debit the item's expense account (COGS) and credit the stock account (Inventory), at the valuation amount. - If the company has "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" enabled (`enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed`), `DeliveryNote.set_expense_account` (around line 463) points `item.expense_account` at the SDBNB account instead. Stock then leaves inventory into an interim account and is not yet COGS. ## 3. Sales Invoice: why COGS isn't booked again - `make_sales_invoice` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py:62` builds the invoice from a Delivery Note. - It uses `get_invoiced_qty_map` and `get_returned_qty_map` to map only the quantity not yet invoiced or returned. - It maps each Delivery Note Item to `dn_detail`, and the parent to `delivery_note`. - It does not turn on `update_stock`, so the invoice does not move stock. - The invoice's general ledger entries come from `SalesInvoice.get_gl_entries`, which calls `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`). - `make_customer_gl_entry` debits the receivable. - `make_item_gl_entries` credits income and tax. - **The COGS and inventory entries are added only if `cint(doc.update_stock)` is set and perpetual inventory is on** (line 374). Only then does it call `super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`, the stock-controller path. - An invoice made from a Delivery Note has `update_stock = 0`, so it adds no COGS and no inventory entries. - The same `update_stock` flag gates the Stock Ledger Entries. `SalesInvoice.on_submit` (around lines 443–453) calls `update_stock_ledger` only `if self.update_stock == 1`. - Other guards keep the two paths from overlapping: - `pos.py` `_set_update_stock_from_profile` sets `update_stock = 0` if any row has `dn_detail`. - `validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` (`sales_invoice.py:353`) stops the same Delivery Note row being billed twice. - `SalesInvoice.check_prev_docstatus` requires the Delivery Note to be submitted. - `set_subcontracted` (`sales_invoice.py:1191`) forces `update_stock = 0` for subcontracted orders. - `SellingController` (line 543) skips item-level stock handling when the invoice has `update_stock = 0`. - **With "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" enabled**, the invoice does post one extra entry pair. `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` runs only when `update_stock` is off and perpetual inventory is on. It looks up the Delivery Note's Stock Ledger Entry through `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item`, then `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` debits COGS and credits SDBNB for `valuation_rate * item.stock_qty`. - COGS is therefore recognised at billing time rather than delivery time, still exactly once. - `_is_sdbnb_reversal` ensures the reversal fires only when the Delivery Note really booked to an SDBNB account. ## 4. Status feedback between the documents - On Delivery Note submit, `BillingStatusService` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/billing_status.py`) runs `update_billing_status`. - If a row has `si_detail` but no `so_detail`, it sets `billed_amt` from the row amount. - If a row has `so_detail`, it calls `update_billed_amount_based_on_so`, which splits invoices billed against the order across Delivery Notes. - It then calls `update_billing_percentage`, which sets `per_billed`. - The Sales Invoice's `status_updater` configuration (around `sales_invoice.py:812`) writes `billed_amt` back to the Sales Order Item and the Delivery Note Item. That is how `per_billed` stays accurate and over-billing is blocked. - The reverse mapping, `make_delivery_note` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/mapper.py:33`, serves invoice-first flows. It maps only `qty - delivered_qty` and skips rows that already have a `dn_detail`, so an invoice that has already been delivered doesn't produce a second delivery.

final answer
In ERPNext the Delivery Note books the cost of goods sold, and the Sales Invoice only does so if it moves the stock itself. A guard stops the invoice from doing both. I read the Delivery Note and Sales Invoice code. I did not open the Sales Order controller or the shared stock base class (`BaseStockGLComposer`), so those parts come from the status-updater config and the search results. **1. Sales Order** - `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/`, with the mapper functions in `mapper.py`. - A Sales Order posts no stock or GL entries. It only reserves stock and tracks progress. - `make_delivery_note` and `make_sales_invoice` in `mapper.py` copy the order into the other documents. They set `so_detail` / `against_sales_order` on the Delivery Note Item and `sales_order` / `so_detail` on the Sales Invoice Item. - `make_sales_invoice` can also set `dn_detail` when invoicing from a Delivery Note. - The `status_updater` config in the Delivery Note and Sales Invoice controllers writes `delivered_qty` and `per_delivered` back to the Sales Order. The Sales Invoice does this only when `update_stock=1`. The Delivery Note also counts invoiced quantity from Sales Invoices that have `update_stock=1`. - The Delivery Note also drives `per_billed` and `billed_amt` through `update_billing_status` and `BillingStatusService`. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, class `DeliveryNote`) - `on_submit` calls `update_prevdoc_status`, `update_billing_status`, `update_stock_ledger` and then `make_gl_entries`. - `update_stock_ledger` creates the Stock Ledger Entries, which are the issue from the warehouse at the item's valuation rate. - `get_gl_entries` hands off to `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` in `delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`. That class inherits the standard stock loop from `BaseStockGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`) and only sets `enforce_pl_expense_account = False`. The loop credits the inventory account and debits the item's `expense_account`. - `validate_expense_account` sets that expense account. If the company has "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" enabled, the debit goes to the `stock_delivered_but_not_billed` account. Otherwise it goes straight to the default COGS account. - It blocks the Stock Delivered But Not Billed account on rows linked to a Sales Invoice (`against_sales_invoice`). **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, class `SalesInvoice`) - `on_submit` calls `update_billing_status_in_dn`, then `update_stock_ledger` (only when `update_stock` is on), then `make_gl_entries`. - `get_gl_entries` hands off to `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose` in `sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`. The composer builds the receivable, tax and income entries, then calls `make_item_gl_entries` and `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries`. **How COGS is booked only once** - **Invoice with `update_stock=0` (the usual case when billing a Delivery Note):** - In `make_item_gl_entries`, the stock and COGS entries are added only if `cint(doc.update_stock)` and perpetual inventory is on. That branch calls `super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`. - With `update_stock=0` the invoice posts only receivable, income and tax. No inventory credit or COGS debit is made, so the Delivery Note's COGS entry is the only one. - **Invoice with `update_stock=1` (no Delivery Note):** the invoice books COGS itself. - **Guard against doing both:** - `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note` is called from `validate`. It throws "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes" if `update_stock` is on and any item has a `delivery_note`. - `validate_expense_account` in the Delivery Note blocks the Stock Delivered But Not Billed account on Delivery Notes created from a Sales Invoice. - `dn_detail` and `si_detail` on the item rows link each line to its counterpart. `update_billing_status_in_dn` uses `dn_detail`, and `against_sales_invoice` / `si_detail` give the reverse link. - **Stock Delivered But Not Billed account (optional, `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed`):** - The Delivery Note debits the Stock Delivered But Not Billed account instead of COGS. - When the invoice is submitted, `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` runs only if `update_stock` is off and perpetual inventory is on. For each invoice item that comes from a Delivery Note, `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` finds the Delivery Note's `expense_account` and the original stock ledger entry (`stock_value_difference / actual_qty`, times the invoice's `stock_qty`). - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` then credits the Stock Delivered But Not Billed account and debits the item's real COGS account for that valuation amount. - The cost therefore reaches COGS at invoice time, and only through this reclassification. The amount comes from the Delivery Note's own stock ledger entry, so it is not recalculated. - `_is_sdbnb_reversal` makes this happen only when the Delivery Note's expense account is a Stock Delivered But Not Billed account that differs from the item's expense account. The reversal is skipped for returns when `disable_sdbnb_in_sr` is set. - **Reposting:** if a Delivery Note's valuation changes, `_update_post_delivery_billed_vouchers` in `repost_item_valuation.py` adds the submitted Sales Invoices linked to it. This keeps the Stock Delivered But Not Billed entries matched.

final answer
COGS is booked once because only one document in the chain ever moves stock. Sales Invoice code blocks a second stock movement against a Delivery Note. I read the code paths below but didn't run any of them. **1. Sales Order** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/`, `mapper.py`) - A Sales Order books nothing in stock or accounting. It only reserves and tracks quantity. - `make_delivery_note` and `make_sales_invoice` (`mapper.py`, around line 425) map the order into the next documents. They carry `so_detail` on each item, and the Delivery Note carries `against_sales_order`. - When a Delivery Note is submitted, `update_prevdoc_status` updates `delivered_qty` and `per_delivered` on the Sales Order. When an invoice is submitted, it updates `billed_amt` and `per_billed`. This is the `status_updater` mechanism in `SellingController` and `StatusUpdater`. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, class `DeliveryNote(SellingController)`) - `on_submit` runs `update_prevdoc_status`, `update_billing_status`, then `update_stock_ledger`, then `make_gl_entries`, then `repost_future_sle_and_gle`. - `update_stock_ledger` writes the outgoing Stock Ledger Entries and the valuation. `SellingController.update_stock_ledger` (`controllers/selling_controller.py`, around line 676) does the work. - `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries` delegates to `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` in `services/gl_composer.py`. That composer posts the standard stock-to-expense entries from `StockController.get_gl_entries` (`controllers/stock_controller.py`): credit Stock In Hand, debit the item's `expense_account`. So the Delivery Note books the cost of goods at submission. - `validate_expense_account` swaps the item's `expense_account` to the company's "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB) account when `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` is set. The debit therefore sits in SDBNB, a balance-sheet account, until the invoice arrives. - `update_billing_status` sets `per_billed` on the Delivery Note. `BillingStatusService` in `services/billing_status.py` does the work and is also called from the invoice. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, class `SalesInvoice(SellingController)`) - When the invoice is created from a Delivery Note, each item row carries `delivery_note` and `dn_detail`. - `on_submit` calls `update_billing_status_in_dn`, which sums billed amounts by `dn_detail` and updates the Delivery Note. It only calls `update_stock_ledger` if `update_stock == 1`. It then calls `make_gl_entries`. - `get_gl_entries` delegates to `SalesInvoiceGLComposer` (`services/gl_composer.py`). - `make_item_gl_entries` posts the receivable, income and tax entries. It adds the stock and COGS entries (`super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`) only when `cint(doc.update_stock)` is set and perpetual inventory is on. - `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` returns immediately if `doc.update_stock` is set. Otherwise, for each stock item with `delivery_note` or `dn_detail`, `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` finds the Delivery Note's SDBNB account. It uses `_is_sdbnb_reversal` to confirm the Delivery Note booked to an account of type "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" that differs from the invoice item's expense account. It then reads the original Stock Ledger Entry for that voucher and `dn_detail`, and takes `stock_value_difference / actual_qty × stock_qty` as the amount. `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` credits SDBNB and debits the item's real COGS account for that amount, so COGS is booked once, at billing. **How double booking is prevented** 1. **No second stock movement.** `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note` throws "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes" if `update_stock` is set and any item has a `delivery_note`. A Delivery Note-linked invoice therefore creates no Stock Ledger Entries and no stock or COGS postings of its own. 2. **Reversal of the Delivery Note's cost, not a new cost.** The amount comes from the Delivery Note's own Stock Ledger Entry, so the invoice moves exactly what was delivered. The net result is Delivery Note: debit SDBNB, credit Stock. Invoice: debit COGS, credit SDBNB. Cost lands in COGS once. 3. **Without SDBNB**, the Delivery Note debits COGS directly. `_is_sdbnb_reversal` is then false, so the invoice adds no cost entry. 4. **Direct invoicing.** If there is no Delivery Note, the invoice sets `update_stock=1` and books the stock and COGS entries itself. A Delivery Note-linked invoice never has `update_stock` set, so only one of the two documents ever moves stock. 5. **Repost and cancel.** - `repost_item_valuation.py::_update_post_delivery_billed_vouchers` reposts invoices created after a Delivery Note, so the SDBNB entries stay matched when valuation changes. - Cancelling a Delivery Note that has a submitted invoice is blocked by `check_next_docstatus`. The invoice's own `make_gl_entries` reverses its GL entries on cancel, and the Delivery Note's `on_cancel` calls `make_gl_entries_on_cancel`.

final answer
Raw materials go out on a Stock Entry, are tracked on the Subcontracting Order's `supplied_items`, and are consumed and costed when the Subcontracting Receipt is submitted. I read most of the code below. I only grepped the names in the Subcontracting Order file and in the `Stock Entry` `on_submit` hook and `BaseStockEntry`, so what they do is inferred from those names. ## 1. Subcontracting Order creates the raw-material list - **Files:** `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` and `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. - `SubcontractingOrder` extends `SubcontractingController`. - In the controller, `validate()` calls `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received()`. It builds the order's `supplied_items` table in this order: - `get_available_materials()` - `_get_materials_from_bom()` (the BOM explosion, with `exploded_item` as an option) - `__add_supplied_or_received_item()` (adds each row) - `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()` (the entry point for the above) - Rates for these rows come from `set_valuation_rate_for_rm()`. - In `SubcontractingOrder`: - `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount()` and `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` total the quantities and amounts. - `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` reserves stock in each row's `reserve_warehouse`. It works through the `Bin` method `update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting`. - `update_status()` sets the order status. The module-level `update_subcontracting_order_status()` does the same from outside the class. - `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po()` and `validate_purchase_order_for_subcontracting()` tie the order back to the Purchase Order. ## 2. Transferring raw materials to the supplier - **Creating the Stock Entry:** `make_rm_stock_entry()` in `subcontracting_controller.py` is whitelisted. It works for a Subcontracting Order, or a Purchase Order via `order_doctype`. - It sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"` and links the order through `subcontracting_order` or `purchase_order`. - It limits the transfer to `required_qty` minus `total_supplied_qty`, with Buying Settings' `over_transfer_allowance` as the cap. - `add_items_in_ste()` adds each row and sets its `sco_rm_detail` (or `po_detail`) link back to the order row. - **Other entry points:** - `get_items_from_subcontract_order()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` is another way to pull the order's items into a Stock Entry. - `get_materials_from_supplier()` and `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract()` in `subcontracting_controller.py` build the return of unused material from the supplier. - **Validation:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` (a `BaseStockEntry` subclass in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`) validates the transfer. - `validate_subcontract_order()` is the main check. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom()` and `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer()` check the BOM and the transfer quantities. - `_validate_transfer_qty()`, `get_total_supplied_qty()` and `get_total_returned_qty()` support them. - `_link_rm_detail_if_missing()` and `get_order_rm_detail()` fill in the row links. - **Tracking against the order:** - On submit and cancel, `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items()` runs. It uses `_get_order_supplied_items()`, `_get_supplied_items_details()` and the module-level `get_supplied_items()`. - `_update_supplied_items_in_order()` writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` onto the order's supplied-item rows with `frappe.db.set_value`. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` then refreshes the reserved quantity on the `Bin`. - **Order status:** `StockEntry.update_subcontracting_order_status` in `stock_entry.py` refreshes the order status. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt: consumption and cost roll-up - **File:** `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. The class `SubcontractingReceipt(SubcontractingController)` is created from the order by `make_subcontracting_receipt()` in `subcontracting_order.py`. - **`validate()`:** - `reset_supplied_items()` rebuilds the raw materials from what was transferred, using `__get_transferred_items`, `__get_received_items` and `__get_consumed_items` in the controller. - It handles backflush with `__get_backflush_based_on`, either the BOM or the material transferred. - `set_missing_values()` calls `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`. - `set_available_qty_for_consumption()` and `get_secondary_items()` handle availability and by-products or scrap. - `set_supplied_items_expense_account()`, `set_supplied_items_cost_center()` and `set_supplied_items_inventory_dimensions()` fill the accounting fields. - **Rate for each raw material:** `update_rate_for_supplied_items()` and `set_rate_for_supplied_items()` in the controller set `rm_obj.rate` with `get_incoming_rate()`. They value the material in `supplier_warehouse` at the quantity consumed. - **Cost roll-up in `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`:** - Each supplied item's `amount` is `consumed_qty * rate`. - The amounts are summed per finished-good row via `reference_name` into `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty`. - Secondary items give `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The finished item's `rate` is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher per qty`. - Rows with a BOM are scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - The method then sets `amount`, `total_qty` and `total`. - `calculate_additional_costs()` and `get_supplied_items_cost()` in the controller feed additional costs and supplied cost. - **`on_submit()` runs these steps in order:** 1. `validate_closed_subcontracting_order()`. 2. `validate_bom_required_qty()`. 3. `update_status_updater_args()` and `update_prevdoc_status()`, which update the received quantities on the order. 4. `set_subcontracting_order_status(update_bin=False)`. 5. `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()`, which writes `consumed_qty` back to the order's `supplied_items` through the private `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`. It caps `consumed_qty` at `supplied_qty`. 6. `update_stock_reservation_entries()`. 7. `update_stock_ledger()`. 8. `make_gl_entries()`. 9. `repost_future_sle_and_gle()`. 10. `update_status()`. 11. `auto_create_purchase_receipt()`. 12. `update_job_card()`. - **Stock ledger posting:** `update_stock_ledger()` in the controller does the following. - It calls `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty()` first. - It adds the finished goods to the receiving warehouse with `incoming_rate` equal to the rolled-up rate and `recalculate_rate = 1`. - It adds rejected quantities to the rejected warehouse. - `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse()` then posts a negative `consumed_qty` for each raw material out of the `supplier_warehouse`. - **Cancel:** `on_cancel()` reverses the same steps. - **GL entries:** `get_gl_entries()` on the receipt builds the accounting entries, and `set_service_expense_account()` and `set_expense_account_for_subcontracted_items()` pick the accounts.

final answer
The flow runs through four stages. I traced it from search results and a few targeted file reads. I did not read every function body end to end, and I did not look at the Subcontracting Order's own `validate`/`on_submit` code beyond what the search results showed. **1. Subcontracting Order (SCO) creates the raw-material requirement** - The class is `SubcontractingOrder` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`. It extends `SubcontractingController` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. - The controller's `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received()` calls `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()`. That builds the "Subcontracting Order Supplied Item" rows (`rm_item_code`, `required_qty`, `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty`, `total_supplied_qty`, `reserve_warehouse`). Its helpers are `__identify_change_in_item_table`, `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` and `__validate_supplied_or_received_items`. - `SubcontractingOrder.calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount()` sets `rm_cost_per_qty` on each item from the BOM. It is called from `set_missing_values`. - `on_submit` calls `reserve_raw_materials()`, which uses `StockReservation` to reserve stock. - `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` updates the bin's reserved quantity. - `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po()` and `update_status()` keep the Purchase Order and the SCO status in sync. **2. Transfer of raw materials to the supplier (Stock Entry, purpose "Send to Subcontractor")** - `make_rm_stock_entry()` in `subcontracting_controller.py` maps the SCO (or a Purchase Order) into a Stock Entry. For each supplied item it sets: - `s_warehouse` to the item's warehouse or `reserve_warehouse`; - `t_warehouse` to the order's `supplier_warehouse`; - `sco_rm_detail` (or `po_detail`) to link the row back to the order; - `main_item_code` and `subcontracted_item` to the finished good. - `make_rm_stock_entry()` also uses `over_transfer_allowance` from Buying Settings to skip items already fully transferred. - `MaterialTransferStockEntry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py` handles the entry on submit and cancel. Both call `update_transferred_qty()` and `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items()`. - `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` does the validation and the write-back to the order: - `validate_subcontract_order()` branches on Buying Settings `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`. - In "BOM" mode it calls `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom()`. That uses `_get_required_qty_for_bom()`, `_validate_transfer_qty()` (required quantity plus allowance, using `get_total_supplied_qty()` and `get_total_returned_qty()`), and `_link_rm_detail_if_missing()`. - In "Material Transferred for Subcontract" mode it calls `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer()`. - `get_order_rm_detail()` finds the order's supplied-item row for a transferred row. - `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items()` recomputes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` on the SCO supplied-item rows. It does this through `get_supplied_items()` and `frappe.db.set_value`, then calls `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()`, which runs `get_bin(...).update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting()`. - The report `subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred.py` shows the pending quantity. Its `get_order_items_to_supply` reads required, supplied and returned quantities. **3. Subcontracting Receipt (SCR) creation and consumption** - `make_subcontracting_receipt()` in `subcontracting_order.py` maps the SCO into a receipt. - `SubcontractingReceipt` is in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. Its supplied-item child is `SubcontractingReceiptSuppliedItem`, which has `consumed_qty`, `rate`, `amount`, `reference_name`, `subcontracting_order` and `bom_detail_no`. - `validate()` runs `reset_supplied_items()`, which in turn calls `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`. That path calls the controller's `get_available_materials()` and `__get_transferred_items`, which work out what was sent to the supplier and not yet consumed. - `__update_consumed_materials` uses `__get_consumed_items` to find what earlier receipts already consumed. `get_materials_from_supplier()` is the related helper. - The rest of `validate()` runs `set_missing_values()`, `get_current_stock()`, `set_supplied_items_expense_account`, `set_supplied_items_cost_center` and `set_supplied_items_inventory_dimensions`. **4. Cost roll-up and reconciliation on SCR submit** - `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit` runs in this order: 1. `validate_closed_subcontracting_order()`. 2. `validate_bom_required_qty()`, which uses `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty()`. 3. `update_status_updater_args()` and `update_prevdoc_status()`. The `status_updater` config updates the SCO's `received_qty` and `per_received` from `Subcontracting Receipt Item.received_qty`, joined on `subcontracting_order`. 4. `set_subcontracting_order_status()`. 5. `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()`. 6. `update_stock_reservation_entries()`. 7. `update_stock_ledger()` and `make_gl_entries()`. GL entries come from `get_gl_entries()`. 8. `repost_future_sle_and_gle()`. 9. `update_status()`. 10. `auto_create_purchase_receipt()` and `update_job_card()`. - `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` does the cost roll-up: - Each supplied item's `amount` is `consumed_qty × rate`, summed per finished-good row via `reference_name` (`rm_cost_map`). - That sum becomes the finished-good row's `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty` (divided by `received_qty` or `qty`). - `secondary_items_cost_per_qty` is also set. It comes from secondary-item rows (those with `secondary_item_type` or `is_legacy_scrap_item`), whose value is spread over the main item's quantity. - The finished good's `rate` is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher amount per qty`. - When the row has a BOM, `amount` is also scaled by `cost_allocation_per`. - `total_qty` and `total` are accumulated. - `SubcontractingController.get_supplied_items_cost()` is a similar helper. - `update_entries_after.update_rate_on_subcontracting_receipt()` in `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py` is called from `update_outgoing_rate_on_transaction`. When the stock ledger revalues the raw-material outgoing rate, it writes the new rate and amount to the "Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item" or "Subcontracting Receipt Item" row. It then calls `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` again, so the finished-good cost follows the real valuation. **Summary:** the flow is `SubcontractingOrder` → `make_rm_stock_entry` → Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor" (`SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`, which updates the order's `supplied_qty`) → `make_subcontracting_receipt` → `SubcontractingReceipt` (consumption, `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`, stock and GL postings) → SCO `per_received`/status update.

final answer
This flow runs through four stages: the Subcontracting Order (SCO), the "Send to Subcontractor" Stock Entry, the SCO's supplied-items tracking, and the Subcontracting Receipt (SCR) with its cost roll-up. I read the key functions in the controller, the SCR and the stock-entry service. I only listed the method names in `subcontracting_order.py` and did not read their bodies. **1. Subcontracting Order: setting up the raw materials** - **File:** `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`, class `SubcontractingOrder`. It extends `SubcontractingController` from `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`, which in turn extends `StockController`. - **Supplied items:** `SubcontractingController.create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received()` builds the `supplied_items` child table (`Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`). The steps are: - `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()` calls `__set_supplied_or_received_items` and `__add_supplied_or_received_item`. - `_get_materials_from_bom` explodes each service item's BOM. - `set_rate_for_supplied_items`/`update_rate_for_supplied_items` set the rate of each raw material. - `set_batch_for_supplied_items` and `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle` assign batches and serial numbers. - **Reservation:** `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin. `validate_supplied_items` and `set_missing_values` check and fill the table. - **Status and Purchase Order:** `update_status`, `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po`, and the module functions `set_subcontracting_order_status` and `update_subcontracting_order_status`. **2. Transfer to the supplier (Stock Entry, purpose "Send to Subcontractor")** - **Creating the entry:** - `make_rm_stock_entry()` in `subcontracting_controller.py` creates the Stock Entry from the SCO's `supplied_items`, or from a Purchase Order. - It sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"` and `subcontracting_order`. - It links each row through `sco_rm_detail` (or `po_detail` for a Purchase Order). - It computes the quantity as required minus already supplied, and enforces `over_transfer_allowance` from Buying Settings. - Its helper `add_items_in_ste` adds the rows. - `get_item_details` supplies default item details and warehouses. - **Return path:** `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` and `get_materials_from_supplier` handle raw materials sent back from the supplier. - **Stock Entry class:** `StockEntry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` holds the `subcontract_data` mapping. This maps `order_field` to `subcontracting_order` and `order_supplied_items_field` to `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`. - It dispatches the purpose "Send to Subcontractor" to `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`. - Related hooks are `validate_closed_subcontracting_order`, `reserve_stock_for_subcontracting`, `update_wo_reservation_for_subcontracting`, `_resolve_subcontract_item` and `update_subcontracting_order_status`. - **Validation and write-back:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` is in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`. - `validate_subcontract_order`, `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` and `_validate_transfer_qty` check that the transfer is allowed. - `get_total_supplied_qty` and `get_total_returned_qty` give the net quantity already sent. - `on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`. - That method calls `_update_supplied_items_in_order` to write `supplied_qty` back to the SCO supplied-items rows. - It also calls `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting`. - The module functions `get_supplied_items` and `get_items_from_subcontract_order` are also in this file. - **Stock effect:** stock moves from the company warehouse to the supplier warehouse (`supplier_warehouse` on the SCO). **3. Receiving finished goods (Subcontracting Receipt)** - **Creating the receipt:** `make_subcontracting_receipt()` in `subcontracting_order.py` maps the SCO to an SCR. - **File:** `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`, class `SubcontractingReceipt(SubcontractingController)`. - **Pulling in the supplied items:** `validate` calls `reset_supplied_items`, and `before_validate` calls `set_items_bom`. `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` then fills the SCR `supplied_items` (`Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item`). - The quantities come from `__get_transferred_items`, `__get_received_items` and `__get_consumed_items`. - These are driven by `get_available_materials`. - The consumption basis is `backflush_based_on`, either BOM or Material Transferred for Subcontract (`__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer`). - `set_available_qty_for_consumption` shows what is available at the supplier. - **Checks:** `validate_bom_required_qty`, `validate_items_qty`, `validate_accepted_warehouse` and `validate_secondary_items`. - **Account and dimension defaults:** `set_supplied_items_cost_center`, `set_supplied_items_expense_account` and `set_supplied_items_inventory_dimensions`. **4. Cost roll-up and reconciliation** - **Rolling up cost:** `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` rolls the cost up in these steps: - For each supplied item, `amount = consumed_qty * rate`. The amounts are summed per FG row through `reference_name` into `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty`. - Secondary items and scrap are summed into `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The FG `rate` is the sum of `rm_cost_per_qty`, `service_cost_per_qty`, `additional_cost_per_qty` and the landed cost voucher amount per qty. - If the row has a BOM, the amount is scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - **Other cost helpers:** `calculate_additional_costs` spreads additional costs by quantity or amount. `get_supplied_items_cost` returns the supplied-item cost for one FG row. - **Submit:** `on_submit` runs these steps in order: 1. `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` 2. `validate_bom_required_qty` 3. `update_status_updater_args` and `update_prevdoc_status` 4. `set_subcontracting_order_status(update_bin=False)`, which refreshes each linked SCO through `sco_doc.update_status` 5. `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, which calls `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` and writes `consumed_qty` back to the SCO supplied items 6. `update_stock_ledger` 7. `make_gl_entries` (the SCR's `get_gl_entries` override feeds this step) 8. `repost_future_sle_and_gle` 9. `update_status` 10. `auto_create_purchase_receipt` 11. `update_job_card` - **Stock ledger:** `update_stock_ledger` in the controller posts these entries. - The finished-goods entry is `+qty` at `incoming_rate = item.rate` with `recalculate_rate`, so the supplied-material cost becomes the valuation. - A rejected quantity goes to the rejected warehouse. - `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` posts `-consumed_qty` of each raw material from `supplier_warehouse`, which consumes the stock held at the supplier. - It also calls `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty`. - **Cancel and return:** `on_cancel` reverses these steps. `is_return` on an SCR reverses the consumption. - **Reporting:** the reports `subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred` and `subcontracted_item_to_be_received`, in `erpnext/buying/report/`, show what is still outstanding.

final answer
I've traced the whole flow and have enough to answer. ## Subcontracting flow: raw materials out, tracked on the Subcontracting Order, costed on the Subcontracting Receipt I did not open every file. The Subcontracting Order's supplied-items population is based on the controller's function list rather than a read of its bodies. The Subcontracting Receipt's `reset_supplied_items` and `update_rate_for_supplied_items` are also from the function list only. I also did not read `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` past a grep of its lines. ### 1. Subcontracting Order (SCO) defines what must be sent - **Files:** `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`, plus the child doctypes `SubcontractingOrderItem`, `SubcontractingOrderServiceItem` and `SubcontractingOrderSuppliedItem`. - **Base class:** `SubcontractingOrder` extends `SubcontractingController` (`erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`), which extends `StockController` and then `AccountsController`. - **Creation:** the SCO is created from a subcontracting Purchase Order. `validate_purchase_order_for_subcontracting` checks that the PO is subcontracted and submitted. - **Supplied items:** `supplied_items` lists the raw materials required per finished good. They are built from the BOM through `SubcontractingController.create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`, `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items`, `get_available_materials` and `_get_materials_from_bom`. - **Supplier warehouse:** `validate_supplied_items` requires `reserve_warehouse` to differ from `supplier_warehouse`. - **Cost estimate:** - `set_missing_values` calls `calculate_additional_costs`, `calculate_service_costs`, `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount` and `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. - `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount` sets `rm_cost_per_qty` from the BOM's item costs. - `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` sets `rate = rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty`. - **Submit:** `on_submit` calls `update_status`, `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po` and `reserve_raw_materials`. The last of these reserves stock when `reserve_stock` is set. - **Ordered and reserved quantities:** `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin for the finished good and for the raw materials in their `reserve_warehouse`. ### 2. Transfer of raw materials to the supplier - **Creating the Stock Entry:** `make_rm_stock_entry` in `subcontracting_controller.py` is whitelisted. It uses `get_mapped_doc` to map the SCO (or the PO) to a Stock Entry. - `post_process` sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"`, links `subcontracting_order`, and calls `set_stock_entry_type`. - It appends one row per remaining quantity: `required_qty - total_supplied_qty`. It skips rows already over-transferred beyond `Buying Settings.over_transfer_allowance`. - Each row has `s_warehouse = rm_item.warehouse or reserve_warehouse` and `t_warehouse = supplier_warehouse`. It also carries `sco_rm_detail`, `main_item_code`, `subcontracted_item` and the serial/batch fields. - Related helpers are `get_item_details`, `add_items_in_ste`, `get_materials_from_supplier` and `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` (returns). - **Stock Entry class:** in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py`, the `StockEntry` class maps the "Send to Subcontractor" purpose to `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`, defined in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`. - The `subcontract_data` dict holds `order_field`, `rm_detail_field` and `order_supplied_items_field`. - `validate` runs `validate_subcontract_order`, `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom`, `_validate_transfer_qty` and `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer`. These use `get_total_supplied_qty` and `get_total_returned_qty` to stop over-transfer. - `_link_rm_detail_if_missing` and `get_order_rm_detail` find the matching SCO supplied-item row. - **Submit:** `StockEntry.on_submit` writes the stock ledger entries, which move stock from the company warehouse to the supplier warehouse. It also calls `reserve_stock_for_subcontracting`, `update_wo_reservation_for_subcontracting` and `update_subcontracting_order_status`. - `update_subcontracting_order_status` calls `set_subcontracting_order_status` from `subcontracting_order.py`. ### 3. Tracking against the SCO - **Service on submit and cancel:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`. - It uses `_get_order_supplied_items`, `_get_supplied_items_details` and `get_supplied_items`. - `get_supplied_items` sums `transfer_qty` per `sco_rm_detail`, separates returns, and computes `total_supplied_qty = supplied_qty - returned_qty`. - `_update_supplied_items_in_order` writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` onto the SCO supplied-item rows. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` refreshes the Bin's reserved quantity for subcontracting. - **Order status:** `set_subcontracting_order_status` and `update_subcontracting_order_status` update the SCO's per-transferred status and percentage. ### 4. Subcontracting Receipt (SCR) receives finished goods and consumes the materials - **File:** `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. `SubcontractingReceipt` extends `SubcontractingController`. Its child doctype `SubcontractingReceiptSuppliedItem` holds the consumed raw materials. - **Creation:** `make_subcontracting_receipt` in `subcontracting_order.py` maps the SCO to an SCR. - **Supplied-items table:** `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` fills the table through `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` and `__set_supplied_or_received_items`. It uses the controller's private helpers: - `__get_transferred_items` (what the supplier holds). - `__get_received_items` and `__get_consumed_items` (what earlier receipts already used). - `__update_consumed_materials`. - `__set_consumed_qty`, `__set_alternative_item`, `__set_batch_nos`, `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle` and `__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer`. Consumption is either BOM-based or based on the material transferred, according to `backflush_based_on` (read from `Buying Settings.backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`). `reset_raw_materials` rebuilds the table. - **Valuation rate:** `set_rate_for_supplied_items` and `update_rate_for_supplied_items` set each row's rate. `set_valuation_rate_for_rm` re-reads the rate with `get_incoming_rate` from the supplier warehouse and recalculates if it changed. - **Cost roll-up:** `SubcontractingReceipt.calculate_items_qty_and_amount` does the roll-up. - For each supplied item, `amount = consumed_qty * rate`. These amounts are summed per `reference_name`, which is the SCR item row. - For each finished item, `rm_supp_cost` is the sum of its raw materials' amounts. `rm_cost_per_qty = rm_supp_cost / (received_qty or qty)`. - `rate = rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher cost per qty`. - Secondary items (by-products and scrap) have their cost deducted through `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - With a BOM, `amount = received_qty * rate * cost_allocation_per / 100`. Totals go to `total_qty` and `total`. - `calculate_additional_costs` distributes additional costs by amount or by quantity. `get_supplied_items_cost` returns the raw-material cost per item row. - **Submit:** `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit` runs these steps: - `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` - `validate_bom_required_qty` - `update_prevdoc_status` - `set_subcontracting_order_status` - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` - `update_stock_reservation_entries` - `update_stock_ledger` - `make_gl_entries` - `repost_future_sle_and_gle` - `update_status` - `auto_create_purchase_receipt` - `update_job_card` - **Reconciling consumption back to the SCO:** `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` sums consumed quantity per `(rm_item_code, main_item_code, SCO)`. `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` writes `consumed_qty` onto the SCO supplied-item rows, capped at `supplied_qty`. - **Stock ledger:** `update_stock_ledger` in the controller books: - `+qty` of finished goods at `item.rate` as the incoming rate, with `recalculate_rate`. - Rejected quantity in the rejected warehouse. - A negative consumed quantity of each raw material in `supplier_warehouse`, from `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse`. It also calls `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty`. - **Accounting:** `get_gl_entries` delegates to `SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer.compose` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`. `_make_item_gl_entries` groups supplied items by `reference_name` and, where `rm_supp_cost` is non-zero, posts the raw-material cost against each finished item. `_make_item_gl_entries_for_lcv` handles landed cost vouchers. - **Cancel:** `on_cancel` reverses the same updates. ### 5. Related paths - `PurchaseReceipt` and `PurchaseInvoice` have their own `PurchaseReceiptItemSupplied` rows. They reuse `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`, which sets `rm_supp_cost` to 0 on the receipt items before recalculating. - `LandedCostTaxesandCharges` feeds the `landed_cost_voucher_amount` used in the receipt's rate.

final answer
The flow runs in three stages. I read the code at each step but did not run it. ## 1. Subcontracting Order (SCO) defines the raw materials needed - `SubcontractingOrder` (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`) holds the "Raw Materials Supplied" table, `supplied_items`. Each row is a `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` with `required_qty`, `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty`, `total_supplied_qty`, `consumed_qty` and `reserve_warehouse`. - `populate_items_table` builds the service items and the `supplied_items` rows from the BOM. Both `SubcontractingOrder.on_submit` and the Stock Entry's `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` also call `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting`. - `calculate_service_costs` sets the service cost per item. - `validate_supplied_items` and `update_status` handle validation and status. `update_status` takes an `update_bin` argument, which controls whether the bin quantities are refreshed. - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin's ordered and reserved quantities for subcontracting. - `SubcontractingController` (`erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`) is the shared base class. `get_available_materials`, `_get_materials_from_bom`, `__add_supplied_or_received_item` and `__set_supplied_or_received_items` build the supplied-items rows. - The "Material Transferred for Subcontract" setting sets how many raw materials the controller backflushes. It is read in `__get_backflush_based_on`, and `__get_transferred_items` uses the transferred quantities in that mode. ## 2. Transfer of raw materials to the supplier - `make_rm_stock_entry` in `subcontracting_controller.py` builds the Stock Entry from the SCO. It sets the purpose to "Send to Subcontractor" and links `subcontracting_order` and `sco_rm_detail`. It works out each quantity as `required_qty − total_supplied_qty` and respects `over_transfer_allowance`. It handles Purchase Orders as well, using `po_detail` and `purchase_order`. Each row is added by `add_items_in_ste`. - `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` creates the return of unused materials. - `MaterialTransferStockEntry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py`) calls `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` from its `on_submit` and `on_cancel`. That hands off to `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`). - **Validation:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` checks the transfer in these methods: - `validate_subcontract_order` is the entry point. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` and `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` cover the two backflush modes. - `_validate_transfer_qty` compares against `get_total_supplied_qty` and `get_total_returned_qty`. - `_link_rm_detail_if_missing` and `get_order_rm_detail` link each row to its SCO row. - **Tracking:** after submit or cancel, `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` runs `_get_order_supplied_items`, `_get_supplied_items_details` and `_update_supplied_items_in_order`. The module-level `get_supplied_items` sums `transfer_qty` per `sco_rm_detail`, separating normal entries from returns. The result is written back to `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` on the SCO rows. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` then calls `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting` on each raw material's reserve warehouse. - The report `erpnext/buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred/...` (`get_order_items_to_supply`) lists what is still pending to send. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt (SCR) consumes the materials and rolls up cost - `make_subcontracting_receipt` and `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt` in `subcontracting_order.py` map the SCO into an SCR. - `SubcontractingReceipt` (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`) extends `SubcontractingController`. - **Status updater:** it updates `Subcontracting Order Item.received_qty` and the SCO's `per_received`. `update_status_updater_args`, `update_prevdoc_status` and `update_status` carry this out. - **`validate`:** - `reset_supplied_items` clears the supplied items. - `super().validate()` runs the controller's validation. - `set_missing_values` calls `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. - `set_supplied_items_expense_account`, `set_supplied_items_cost_center` and `set_supplied_items_inventory_dimensions` fill in the accounting fields. - `get_current_stock` and `set_available_qty_for_consumption` set the available quantities. - **Setting up consumption:** `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` and `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` build the `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item` rows (`consumed_qty`, `rate`, `amount`, `reference_name`). `set_batch_for_supplied_items` and `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle` handle batch and serial numbers. - **Cost of raw materials:** `set_valuation_rate_for_rm` calls `get_incoming_rate` for the supplier warehouse. `set_rate_for_supplied_items` and `update_rate_for_supplied_items` set the rate per row. - **Additional costs:** `calculate_additional_costs` spreads `additional_costs` over the items into `additional_cost_per_qty`, either by Qty or by Amount. - **Cost roll-up:** `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` sums each finished item's `consumed_qty × rate` into `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty`. It then sets the finished item's rate as follows: `rate = rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher cost per qty` Secondary and scrap items take their cost out of the main item, and `BOM.cost_allocation_per` is applied when the row has a BOM. It also sets `total` and `total_qty`. - **`on_submit`:** - `validate_bom_required_qty` and `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` run first. The latter calls `__update_consumed_materials` and `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, which write `consumed_qty` back onto the SCO supplied-item rows, capped at `supplied_qty`. - `update_stock_ledger` (controller) runs next. It posts a positive SLE for each finished item with `incoming_rate = item.rate`, and a rejected-warehouse SLE if there is a rejected quantity. `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` posts negative SLEs for the consumed raw materials from `supplier_warehouse`. `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty` refreshes the ordered and reserved quantities. - `make_gl_entries` calls `get_gl_entries`, which uses `SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer` (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`). The composer builds: - the debit to the stock account for each finished item; - the service-cost credit; - the raw-material credit from the supplier warehouse; - the additional-cost and landed-cost-voucher entries; - the divisional loss. `_make_item_gl_entries` and `_make_item_gl_entries_for_lcv` build these entries. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `update_status`, `auto_create_purchase_receipt` and `update_job_card` finish the submit. - **`on_cancel`** reverses these steps. A return SCR (`is_return`) restores the raw materials to the supplier warehouse.

final answer
**Overview:** the flow has three stages. A "Send to Subcontractor" Stock Entry moves the raw materials. The Subcontracting Order tracks what was supplied. The Subcontracting Receipt consumes the supplied materials and rolls their cost into the finished good. I read the key functions, but I did not read every one in full. In particular, I did not read `StockEntry.on_submit`, and I did not open `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt`, `reserve_raw_materials`, `update_rate_for_supplied_items` or `set_rate_for_supplied_items`. ## 1. Subcontracting Order: the demand side - **Class and file:** `SubcontractingOrder(SubcontractingController)` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`. - **Base controller:** `SubcontractingController(StockController)` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. - **Building the supplied-items table:** `validate` and `on_submit` build the `supplied_items` ("Raw Materials Supplied") table. The table holds `rm_item_code`, `main_item_code`, `required_qty`, `supplied_qty`, `consumed_qty`, `reserve_warehouse` and `total_supplied_qty`. - `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` and `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` drive the building. - `_get_materials_from_bom` explodes the BOM to get the required raw materials. - `__set_supplied_or_received_items` and `__add_supplied_or_received_item` add the rows. - **Backflush setting:** the Buying Settings option `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on` chooses between "BOM" and "Material Transferred for Subcontract". - **Order-level methods:** - `populate_items_table` and `calculate_service_costs` fill the items and the service cost. - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin quantities. - `reserve_raw_materials` creates Stock Reservation Entries. - `update_status` and `set_subcontracting_order_status` maintain the order status. - `validate_purchase_order_for_subcontracting`, `validate_service_items` and `validate_supplied_items` are the validations. ## 2. Transfer of raw materials to the supplier - **Creating the Stock Entry:** `make_rm_stock_entry` in `subcontracting_controller.py` builds the Stock Entry from the order. It sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"`, links `subcontracting_order` (or `purchase_order`) and fills each row's `sco_rm_detail` (or `po_detail`). - It computes the quantity per row as `required_qty - total_supplied_qty`, and it respects `over_transfer_allowance`. - `add_items_in_ste` appends the rows, and `get_item_details` supplies the item defaults. - The same file has `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` for returning materials, and `get_materials_from_supplier` for a supplier-sent flow. - **Stock Entry type:** `StockEntryType` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry_type/stock_entry_type.py` defines the "Send to Subcontractor" purpose. - **Validation:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` handles this. - `validate_subcontract_order` branches on the backflush setting. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` checks the over-transfer allowance. It calls `_get_required_qty_for_bom`, `_validate_transfer_qty` and `_link_rm_detail_if_missing`. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` requires `subcontracted_item` and links the order row through `get_order_rm_detail`. - `get_total_supplied_qty` and `get_total_returned_qty` sum quantities from earlier submitted Stock Entries. - **Tracking back to the order:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`. - That method calls `_get_order_supplied_items`, then `_get_supplied_items_details` (which uses `get_supplied_items`), then `_update_supplied_items_in_order`. - `_update_supplied_items_in_order` writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` onto the order's supplied-items rows. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` then calls `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting`. - `MaterialTransferStockEntry.update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py` calls this same method. That handles returns, which are Material Transfers. - **Reservations:** - `StockEntry.reserve_stock_for_subcontracting` (in `stock_entry.py`) calls `SubcontractingOrder.reserve_raw_materials` when the order has `reserve_stock` set. - `StockEntry.update_wo_reservation_for_subcontracting` calls `WorkOrderStockReservation.release_reserved_qty_for_subcontract_transfer`. That frees the Work Order's own reservation. It reads `_subcontract_transferred_qty_by_item` in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/reservation.py`. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt: consumption and cost roll-up - **Class and file:** `SubcontractingReceipt(SubcontractingController)` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. - **Creating the receipt:** `make_subcontracting_receipt` calls `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt` in `subcontracting_order.py`. - **Child tables:** - The supplied rows are `SubcontractingReceiptSuppliedItem` documents with `consumed_qty`, `rate`, `amount`, `reference_name` and `available_qty_for_consumption`. - The `items` table holds `rm_supp_cost`, `rm_cost_per_qty`, `service_cost_per_qty`, `additional_cost_per_qty` and `landed_cost_voucher_amount`. - **Validate path:** `validate` calls `reset_supplied_items` and then `super().validate()`. After that it calls `set_missing_values`, `set_available_qty_for_consumption`, `get_current_stock` and the `set_supplied_items_*` methods for expense account, cost center and inventory dimensions. - The controller's `set_valuation_rate_for_rm`, `update_rate_for_supplied_items` and `set_rate_for_supplied_items` set the raw-material rates. - `get_available_materials`, `__get_transferred_items` and `__update_consumed_materials` work out what was transferred and how much is consumed. - `__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer` and `__set_consumed_qty` set the consumption quantity. - `set_batch_for_supplied_items` sets batches on the supplied rows. - `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle` creates bundles for the supplied rows. - **Cost roll-up:** `SubcontractingReceipt.calculate_items_qty_and_amount` does the roll-up. - For each supplied row, `amount = consumed_qty * rate`. It sums these per finished-good row through `reference_name`, which gives `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty`. - Secondary items and scrap are subtracted through `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The finished good's rate is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + lcv_cost_per_qty`. - If the row has a BOM, the amount is scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - `calculate_additional_costs` in the controller distributes additional costs by Amount or Qty into `additional_cost_per_qty`. - `get_supplied_items_cost` is a helper that sums the supplied-item amounts for one finished-good row. - **On submit:** - `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` and `validate_bom_required_qty` run first. - `update_status_updater_args` and `update_prevdoc_status` update the received quantity on the order. - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` writes the consumed quantity back to the order's supplied-items rows through `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`. It caps each row at `supplied_qty`. - `update_stock_reservation_entries` updates the reservations. - `update_stock_ledger` posts the stock ledger entries. - `make_gl_entries` posts the accounts. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle` reposts later entries. - `update_status`, `auto_create_purchase_receipt` and `update_job_card` finish the submit. - **Stock ledger:** `SubcontractingController.update_stock_ledger` posts the finished good to the item's warehouse with `incoming_rate = item.rate` and `recalculate_rate = 1`. It also posts rejected quantities to the rejected warehouse. - `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` posts `-consumed_qty` for each raw material out of `supplier_warehouse`. That is how the stock held at the supplier is reconciled. - **General ledger:** `SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` builds the entries. `SubcontractingReceipt.get_gl_entries` calls it, and `_make_item_gl_entries` does the main work. - It debits the inventory account by the `stock_value_difference` read from the finished good's Stock Ledger Entry. - It credits the item's `expense_account` with `stock_value_diff - service_cost`. That is the raw-material portion. - It credits `service_expense_account` (falling back to `expense_account`) with `service_cost_per_qty * qty`. - The function continues further (for example additional costs and supplied-item entries). I did not read that part. - **Landed cost:** a Landed Cost Voucher adds `landed_cost_voucher_amount` to the item, which feeds into the rate in `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. The controller's `update_stock_ledger` has a `via_landed_cost_voucher` parameter for this.
