final answer
A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) spreads its charges across the receipt items first. On submit it then rewrites each linked receipt's valuation rate, stock ledger and GL entries in place. I read the code paths below but didn't run any of this. ## 1. Spreading charges across items This happens in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, in the `LandedCostVoucher` class. - **Item rows.** `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` pulls the receipt items into the LCV's `items` table, using `get_pr_items()`. - **Total charges.** `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` sums `base_amount` over the `taxes` table. That table holds the freight and customs rows, each with an expense account. - **Per-item split.** `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` runs unless `distribute_charges_based_on` is "Distribute Manually". - The basis field can be Qty, Amount or similar. Each item gets `applicable_charges = item[basis] * total_taxes_and_charges / sum(basis)`. - Any rounding difference goes onto the last item row. - **Manual mode.** With "Distribute Manually", the user types `applicable_charges` themselves. - **Check on submit.** `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` requires the item charges to add up to `total_taxes_and_charges`, within a rounding tolerance. It throws an error otherwise. ## 2. Retroactively updating the submitted receipts This is `LandedCostVoucher.update_landed_cost()`. `on_submit` calls it, and so does `on_cancel`. It works in two passes over the `purchase_receipts` rows. These rows can point to a Purchase Receipt, Purchase Invoice, Subcontracting Receipt or Stock Entry. **Pass 1: valuation rate** - It loads each receipt document. - It calls `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`, a module-level function. For each receipt item it sums `Landed Cost Item.applicable_charges` over all submitted LCVs (`docstatus == 1`). It matches on `receipt_document` and `purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item` for Stock Entries). The sum is stored in `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount`. Because it sums only submitted LCVs, cancelling an LCV drops its share automatically. - It calls `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`, defined in `BuyingController` in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`. The new rate is `(base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom`. For a Subcontracting Receipt it calls `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - It saves the changes with `item.db_update()` on each item, so the submitted document is not re-saved. - For non-asset items it calls `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()`, which sets `Serial No.purchase_rate` to the new valuation rate. **Pass 2: stock ledger and GL entries** For each receipt, the code: 1. Sets `docstatus = 2`, then calls `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` and `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`. This reverses the old stock ledger and GL entries. 2. Sets `docstatus = 1` and calls `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. 3. Calls `update_stock_ledger(...)` again to post new stock ledger entries at the new valuation rate. 4. Calls `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` for a Purchase Receipt, or plain `make_gl_entries()` for the other types. 5. Calls `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. This revalues later transactions. It runs through `StockLedgerService` and the repost helpers in `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, which also set `via_landed_cost_voucher` on the Repost Item Valuation entry. ## 3. How the GL entries pick up the charges - `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries()` passes `via_landed_cost_voucher` to `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()`. That class is in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`. - The composer's item loop uses `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` in the stock-in-hand debit. That is the amount that raises inventory value. - `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` in `landed_cost_voucher.py` builds a map keyed by `(item_code, receipt item name)` and then by expense account. It reads the submitted LCVs from `Landed Cost Purchase Receipt` and the LCV `taxes` rows, and splits each account's amount in proportion to the item's share. - The composer's `make_landed_cost_gl_entries()` uses that map to credit the freight or customs expense accounts, using `base_amount`. - `make_expenses_added_to_stock_entries()` handles the optional "Expenses Included In Valuation" pairing. - Fixed-asset items (`is_fixed_asset`) get separate handling, and `validate_asset_qty_and_status()` blocks the LCV if the related assets are already submitted.

A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) does two jobs. It splits its charges across the receipt lines, and on submit it rebuilds the stock and GL postings of the receipts it points at. The main file is `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`. I read the code but did not run it. ## 1. Distributing charges across line items **`LandedCostVoucher.validate()`** drives the setup: - `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` calls `get_pr_items()` and fills the `items` table (Landed Cost Item). Each row carries qty, amount, `receipt_document`, and `purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item`). - `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` sets the voucher total to the sum of `base_amount` over the `taxes` rows (the freight, customs and similar charges). - `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` does the split. The basis is `distribute_charges_based_on`, which is Qty, Amount or Distribute Manually. - Each row gets `applicable_charges = row[basis] * total_taxes_and_charges / sum(basis over all rows)`. - Any rounding difference is added to the last row. - If the voucher is set to Distribute Manually, this step is skipped and the user's values are kept. - It throws an error if the basis totals zero. **`on_submit()`** first calls `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`. That check confirms the per-row `applicable_charges` add up to `total_taxes_and_charges`. A rounding gap within tolerance is absorbed into the last row. A larger gap raises an error. ## 2. Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts `on_submit()` and `on_cancel()` both call **`update_landed_cost()`**. It runs two passes over `purchase_receipts`. **Pass 1: valuation rate** - It loads each submitted receipt with `frappe.get_doc`. - **`set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`** sets `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` on each receipt row. The value is the sum of `applicable_charges` from all submitted (`docstatus=1`) Landed Cost Items that reference that row. Cancelling an LCV therefore drops its share automatically. - **`BuyingController.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`** in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py` recomputes the rate: `valuation_rate = (base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / (qty * conversion_factor)`. Subcontracting Receipts use `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - `item.db_update()` writes the new values straight to the database, with no resubmit. - `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` refreshes the rate on serial numbers. Stock Entries and Subcontracting Receipts skip this step. **Pass 2: stock ledger and GL** - It sets `docstatus = 2` on the loaded doc and calls `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. This reverses the old Stock Ledger Entries. - It then calls `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`, which reverses the old GL entries. - It sets `docstatus = 1` and calls `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. It calls `update_stock_ledger(...)` again. These are re-posted at the new valuation rate. - For a Purchase Receipt it calls `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. Other receipt types call `make_gl_entries()`. ## 3. How the GL entries get the landed-cost split - For a Purchase Receipt, `get_gl_entries()` calls `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`. - The composer uses `doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()`. That method is defined in `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py` and delegates to `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` in the LCV file. - That function rebuilds a map of `(item_code, receipt_item_name) → expense_account → {amount, base_amount}`. It loops over every submitted LCV that touches the receipt and splits each tax row's amount in proportion to the row's share of the basis. - The composer's inner `make_landed_cost_gl_entries(item)` uses that map. It credits each LCV expense account, such as "Expenses Included In Valuation", and the stock-in-hand amount includes `landed_cost_voucher_amount`.

A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) spreads its charges across receipt items in two steps. It first allocates the charges to its own item rows, then reposts each linked receipt so the extra cost enters stock valuation and the GL. The main code is in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, class `LandedCostVoucher`. I read that file and part of `buying_controller.py`. I did not read the GL composer functions, and I did not run anything. **1. Redistributing the charges across items** - `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` fills the LCV `items` table (child doctype `Landed Cost Item`). It uses `get_pr_items()` to pull the lines of each linked receipt. - `validate()` sums the `taxes` rows (`Landed Cost Taxes and Charges`) into `total_taxes_and_charges`, using `set_total_taxes_and_charges()`. - `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` does the allocation. - Unless `distribute_charges_based_on` is "Distribute Manually", it totals the chosen basis field across all rows. The basis is Qty, Amount, or Distribute Manually. - Each row's `applicable_charges` is `row_basis × total_taxes_and_charges / total_basis`. - Any rounding difference goes onto the last row. - It throws an error if the total basis is zero. - `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` runs on submit. It checks that the row charges add up to `total_taxes_and_charges`, within a rounding tolerance. This matters most for manual distribution. **2. Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts** `on_submit()` calls `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`, then `update_landed_cost()`, then `update_claimed_landed_cost()`. `on_cancel()` calls `update_landed_cost()` again, so cancelling reverses the effect. `update_landed_cost()` works in two passes over `purchase_receipts`. It can handle Purchase Receipt, Purchase Invoice, Subcontracting Receipt, and Stock Entry. *First pass, which updates the receipt's data:* - `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` is a module-level function in the same file. For each receipt item, it sums `Landed Cost Item.applicable_charges` from submitted LCVs (docstatus 1) that match the receipt and item row. It matches on `purchase_receipt_item`, or on `stock_entry_item` for a Stock Entry. The sum goes into `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount`. - `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` is in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`. It recomputes `item.valuation_rate` as `(base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / (qty × conversion_factor)`. Subcontracting Receipts use `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - `item.db_update()` saves the changed item rows directly to the database, so the already-submitted receipt is not re-validated. - `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` writes the new valuation rate to each Serial No's `purchase_rate`. Stock Entries and Subcontracting Receipts skip this step. *Second pass, which reposts the ledgers:* 1. The receipt is loaded and `docstatus` is set to 2. Then `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` and `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` reverse the old stock ledger and GL entries. 2. `docstatus` is set back to 1. Then `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` and `update_stock_ledger(...)` re-post stock at the new valuation rate. 3. `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` re-posts the GL for a Purchase Receipt. Other receipt types call `make_gl_entries()` without that flag. 4. `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` updates later stock ledger and GL entries that depend on this receipt's valuation. **GL account split** - `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` and `has_landed_cost_amount()` in the same file build a per-item, per-account map of landed-cost amounts. The map comes from the LCV tax rows' expense accounts. The receipt's GL composer uses it to credit those accounts and debit stock. - `validate_expense_accounts()` checks that those accounts belong to the right company. `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` also takes `via_landed_cost_voucher` and passes it down to the serial/batch bundle handling.

final answer
A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) first spreads its charges across line items. On submit it then rewrites the already-submitted receipts' stock and GL entries in place. **Main file:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, class `LandedCostVoucher`. ## 1. Distributing charges across items - **Collecting items.** `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` (also called from `validate()` when no items exist) pulls each receipt's item rows via `get_pr_items`. For each row it copies `qty`, `rate`, `amount` and `cost_center`, plus the link back to the source row (`purchase_receipt_item`, or `stock_entry_item` for Stock Entry). - **Totalling charges.** `validate()` calls `set_total_taxes_and_charges()`, which sums `base_amount` over the `taxes` table (freight, customs and so on). - **Spreading the total.** `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` then runs, unless `distribute_charges_based_on` is "Distribute Manually". - The basis field is `frappe.scrub(distribute_charges_based_on)`, which is `qty`, `amount` or similar. - Each item gets `applicable_charges = item[basis] * total_taxes_and_charges / total_item_cost`. - Any rounding difference goes onto the last item. - It throws if the basis total is zero. - **Checking on submit.** `on_submit()` first calls `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`, which matters mostly for manual distribution. It checks that the sum of `applicable_charges` equals `total_taxes_and_charges`. It tolerates a small rounding difference by adjusting the last row, and throws otherwise. ## 2. Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts `on_submit()` and `on_cancel()` both call `update_landed_cost()`, which has two loops over `purchase_receipts`. **Loop 1: valuation rate** - It loads each receipt with `frappe.get_doc(receipt_document_type, receipt_document)`. - `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` (module-level) sums `applicable_charges` from submitted `Landed Cost Item` rows for each receipt item. It matches on `purchase_receipt_item` or `stock_entry_item` and writes the sum to `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount`. Because it sums over all submitted LCVs, cancelling an LCV removes its share. - `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` is in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`. It recomputes: `valuation_rate = (base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom`. Subcontracting Receipt uses `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - `item.db_update()` persists the new amounts directly on the submitted document's rows. - For receipts other than Stock Entry and Subcontracting Receipt, `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` updates the rate on serial numbers. **Loop 2: stock ledger and GL entries** - The receipt's `docstatus` is temporarily set to 2. Then `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` and `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` reverse the old entries. - It then sets `docstatus = 1` and calls `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. After that it calls `update_stock_ledger(..., via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` again. - `update_stock_ledger` is in `buying_controller.py`. - It goes through `StockController.make_sl_entries`, `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries` and `make_sl_entries` in `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`. - `make_entry` sets `sle.via_landed_cost_voucher`. - This repost writes new Stock Ledger Entries whose incoming rate includes the LCV share, because the item's `valuation_rate` now includes it. - `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` is used for Purchase Receipt. Other receipt types call `make_gl_entries()` with no arguments. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` is in `StockController` and `StockLedgerService`. It creates a `Repost Item Valuation` record, so later transactions in the same item/warehouse get their valuation and GL recomputed. **How the GL postings pick up the charge** - `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries` delegates to `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`. - The composer calls `doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()`, which is defined in `stock_controller.py`. That wraps the module-level `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` in the LCV file. - That function finds the submitted LCVs linked to the receipt through `Landed Cost Purchase Receipt`. For each item and each LCV tax row's `expense_account`, it computes the share as `account.amount * item[basis] / total_item_cost` (or `applicable_charges / exchange_rate` when the total is zero). - The composer's `make_landed_cost_gl_entries` then credits those expense accounts. It also adds `landed_cost_voucher_amount` to the Stock In Hand debit and to the item's stock value. Fixed assets with an LCV amount are handled separately in the same composer. - The Stock Entry, Subcontracting Receipt and Purchase Invoice composers have equivalent code. I did not trace what `RepostItemValuation` does after it is created.

A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) works in two stages. It first splits the charges across the receipt lines, then re-books the receipts that were already submitted. Almost all of this lives in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`. I read the code and did not run it. ## 1. Redistributing charges across line items - **Loading the lines.** `LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` calls `get_pr_items()` for each row in `purchase_receipts`. It builds the `items` table (Landed Cost Item rows) with `qty`, `rate`, `amount`, `receipt_document`, and a link back to the source row. That link is `purchase_receipt_item`, or `stock_entry_item` for Stock Entries. - **Total charges.** `validate()` calls `set_total_taxes_and_charges()`, which sums the `base_amount` of the `taxes` rows. These are the freight and customs rows. - **The split.** `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` is called from `validate()`. - It picks the field named by `distribute_charges_based_on` (Qty or Amount) and sums it over all `items`. - Each line gets `applicable_charges = item_value × total_taxes_and_charges / total_item_value`, rounded to the field's precision. - Any rounding difference is added to the last line. - It throws an error if the total is zero. - With "Distribute Manually" the user's own `applicable_charges` values are kept. - **Front-end copy.** The same split runs in the browser as `set_applicable_charges_for_item()` in `landed_cost_voucher.js`. - **Submit check.** `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` runs from `on_submit`. It checks that the line charges add up to `total_taxes_and_charges`. It tolerates a small rounding difference and puts that difference on the last row. ## 2. Retroactively updating submitted receipts `on_submit` and `on_cancel` both call `update_landed_cost()`. `on_cancel` runs the same code, so cancelling an LCV removes its charges from the receipts the same way. **First pass, per receipt:** - `validate_asset_qty_and_status()` runs if the voucher is not being cancelled. It checks that enough Assets exist for fixed-asset lines and that none are submitted yet. - `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` sets each receipt row's `landed_cost_voucher_amount`. It sums `applicable_charges` from submitted Landed Cost Item rows that match that receipt row. Because it sums every submitted LCV, multiple vouchers on one receipt accumulate, and a cancelled one drops out. - `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` is `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`. It computes `valuation_rate = (base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / stock_qty`. - Subcontracting Receipts call `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - Stock Entry has its own `update_valuation_rate`, which uses `additional_cost + landed_cost_voucher_amount`. - `item.db_update()` saves those fields on the already-submitted document without a normal save. - `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` writes the new `valuation_rate` to `Serial No.purchase_rate`. Stock Entries and Subcontracting Receipts skip this step. **Second pass, re-posting each receipt:** - It sets `docstatus = 2` and calls `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. This goes through `make_sl_entries`, `StockLedgerService` and `stock_ledger_entry.py`. It also calls `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`. Together these reverse the old Stock Ledger and GL entries. - It sets `docstatus = 1` and calls `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. It then calls `update_stock_ledger(...)` again, which writes Stock Ledger entries at the new valuation rate. - For a Purchase Receipt it calls `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`, which goes to `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose`. Other receipt types call `make_gl_entries()`. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` (in `stock_controller.py` and `StockLedgerService`) creates a Repost Item Valuation. That recalculates later transactions, such as issues made after the receipt and their COGS. **GL postings.** `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` builds an account-wise map for the receipt. The receipt's GL composer uses it to split the landed-cost amount by each LCV tax row's `expense_account`. - It is skipped unless `has_landed_cost_amount(doc)` is true. - It reads the `Landed Cost Purchase Receipt` rows of submitted LCVs that point at the receipt. - For each LCV it computes each item's share against the LCV's distribution basis, using `taxes.expense_account`, `base_amount` and `exchange_rate`. - The Purchase Receipt GL composer (`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose`) then adds credits to the "Expenses Included in Valuation" style account, and raises the stock-in-hand debit to match. The Subcontracting Receipt composer (`gl_composer.py`, around line 224) uses the same landed-cost entries. The GL composer code itself, and the rest of `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`, I did not read in full.

final answer
A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) first splits its charges across its own item rows. On submit it then rewrites the landed-cost amount and valuation rate on each linked receipt, cancels and re-posts that receipt's ledger entries, and reposts later transactions. I read this in the code but did not run it. **1. Distributing charges across line items** All of this is in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, in the `LandedCostVoucher` class. - `set_total_taxes_and_charges` sums the `base_amount` of the charges table into `total_taxes_and_charges`. - `set_applicable_charges_on_item` runs during `validate`. The voucher's items are pulled from the receipts by `get_items_from_purchase_receipts`. - It reads the field named by `distribute_charges_based_on`, which is Qty, Amount or Distribute Manually. - Each item gets `applicable_charges = item_value × total_taxes_and_charges / sum(item_values)`, rounded to the field's precision. - Any rounding difference is added to the last item. - It throws an error if the total is zero. - Manual distribution skips this step. - `validate_applicable_charges_for_item` runs on submit. It checks that the item charges add up to the total, and it absorbs a tiny rounding gap into the last row. - `landed_cost_voucher.js` has a client-side copy of the same logic, `set_applicable_charges_for_item`. **2. Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts** `on_submit` calls `update_landed_cost`, and `on_cancel` calls it too. It handles each receipt in two passes. First pass, per linked receipt (Purchase Receipt, Subcontracting Receipt or Stock Entry): - `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` sums `applicable_charges` from all submitted Landed Cost Item rows for each receipt item. It matches on `purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item`) and writes the total to `landed_cost_voucher_amount`. - `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` is in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`. It recomputes each item's rate as `(base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / (qty × conversion_factor)`. Subcontracting Receipts use `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - `item.db_update()` saves the changed items directly, without re-submitting the document. - `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items` updates the rate on serial numbers, except for Stock Entry and Subcontracting Receipt. Second pass, per receipt: - The code sets `docstatus = 2` and calls `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`, then `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`. This reverses the old stock ledger and GL entries. - It then sets `docstatus = 1` and calls `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` and `update_stock_ledger(...)` again to post new stock ledger entries at the new rate. - For a Purchase Receipt it calls `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. The other receipt types call `make_gl_entries()`. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` reposts later transactions so their valuation follows the new rate. The `via_landed_cost_voucher` flag is passed down through these layers: - `StockController` in `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py` - `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` - `make_sl_entries` in `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py` - `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle` in `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py` It lets the cancel-and-repost go through even with negative stock, and it stops the serial/batch bundles being treated as new. **3. GL postings** The Purchase Receipt's GL composer is in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` and is reached through `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries`. - It adds `landed_cost_voucher_amount` to the stock value it debits. - It splits the LCV amounts by expense account using `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries` (`get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` in the LCV module). That function reads the submitted Landed Cost Purchase Receipt links and their voucher items. It spreads each charge across the receipt items in proportion to the same basis. - The matching credits go to the LCV's expense accounts, for example "expenses included in valuation". On cancel, `update_landed_cost` runs again. `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` now ignores the cancelled voucher, so the amounts and ledger entries are rebuilt without it.

final answer
ERPNext restricts these endpoints with the `methods` argument of Frappe's `@frappe.whitelist` decorator. Writing `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` makes the endpoint accept only POST. I found this by grepping the decorator usages and reading the function names beneath them. I did not open Frappe itself, so the enforcement description below comes from how the decorator is known to behave, not from code I read here. **How it works** - A plain `@frappe.whitelist()` exposes a function over `/api/method/...` for any HTTP verb, including GET. - With `methods=[...]`, Frappe checks the request's HTTP method before running the function. If the method isn't in the list, the request is rejected with a `PermissionError` (HTTP 403 or 405). - GET requests are the ones that can be triggered by a link, an `<img>` tag or a cross-site request. They also skip CSRF-token protection and don't open a database write transaction. Limiting write endpoints to POST closes off those routes. - In this codebase the restriction is used consistently on state-changing endpoints. Read-only endpoints that need an explicit allow-list use `methods=["GET"]`. Examples are two functions in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py`, at lines 388 and 900. **Concrete POST-only endpoints** - `erpnext/projects/doctype/task/task.py`: - `set_multiple_status` - `add_node` - `add_multiple_tasks` - `erpnext/projects/doctype/project/project.py`: - `create_duplicate_project` - `set_project_status` - `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py`: `make_work_orders`. - `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py`: `make_purchase_receipt`. - `erpnext/buying/doctype/request_for_quotation/mapper.py`: `create_supplier_quotation`. - `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/lead.py`: `add_lead_to_prospect`. - `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/mapper.py`: `make_lead_from_communication`. - `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/mapper.py`: `make_opportunity_from_communication`. - `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`: `make_quality_inspections`. - `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py`: `update_company_master_and_address`. - `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py`: the `get_customer_group_details` method on the `Customer` class. - The bank reconciliation tool file, which has many POST-restricted functions. - Other files that carry the same decorator: - `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py` - `erpnext/support/doctype/issue/issue.py` - `erpnext/assets/doctype/location/location.py` - `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py` - `erpnext/erpnext_integrations/doctype/plaid_settings/plaid_settings.py` - `erpnext/www/banking.py` My search output was capped at 40 matches, so there are probably more endpoints with this restriction than the ones listed.

final answer
ERPNext blocks GET on these endpoints by passing an allowed-methods list to Frappe's whitelist decorator: `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])`. I found the usages with a repo-wide grep and read the decorated function names from the source. I did not open Frappe's source, so the enforcement description below comes from my knowledge of Frappe. **Mechanism** - `frappe.whitelist` records the allowed HTTP verbs for the function, which defaults to all of them. `methods=["POST"]` narrows that to POST only. - When a request arrives at `/api/method/<dotted.path>`, Frappe's request handler checks the request verb against the function's allowed list before calling it. A GET request is rejected with a `PermissionError`/405-style error, so the function body never runs. - This stops state-changing calls from being triggered by a plain GET, such as a link or an `<img>` tag. It is also tied to CSRF protection, because POST requests need a CSRF token. - Some of these endpoints also use `allow_guest=True`, for example `erpnext/www/banking.py` and `erpnext/templates/utils.py`. For those, the POST restriction matters even more. **Concrete endpoints with `methods=["POST"]`** - `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/lead.py`: `add_lead_to_prospect` - `erpnext/projects/doctype/task/task.py`: `set_multiple_status`, `add_node`, `add_multiple_tasks` - `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py`: `set_work_order_ops` - `erpnext/selling/page/point_of_sale/point_of_sale.py`: `create_opening_voucher`, `set_customer_info` - `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`: `make_quality_inspections` - `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py`: `update_company_master_and_address` - `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py`: `add_node`, `create_transaction_deletion_request` - `erpnext/stock/doctype/batch/batch.py`: `split_batch` Other files in the grep output use the same decorator: - `crm/doctype/lead/mapper.py`, `crm/doctype/opportunity/opportunity.py` and `crm/doctype/opportunity/mapper.py` - `selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py` - `buying/doctype/request_for_quotation/mapper.py` - `stock/doctype/warehouse/warehouse.py` and `stock/doctype/material_request/material_request.py` - `erpnext_integrations/doctype/plaid_settings/plaid_settings.py` - `accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py` The grep output was capped at 40 lines, so there are likely more. The same decorator is also applied to some class methods, such as `Customer`, `Workstation` and `Issue` methods.

ERPNext restricts these endpoints with the `methods` argument of Frappe's whitelist decorator. State-changing endpoints are declared as `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])`. I found this by grepping the decorator. I did not read Frappe's source, so the enforcement description below comes from how Frappe works, not from this repo. **Mechanism** - A plain `@frappe.whitelist()` endpoint accepts any HTTP verb, GET included. - Passing `methods=["POST"]` records the allowed verbs for that function. - Frappe's request handler (`frappe.handler` / `frappe.is_whitelisted`) checks the verb of each `/api/method/...` call against that list. A GET request to such an endpoint is rejected with a `PermissionError` (HTTP 405 or 403), so a state change can't be triggered through a link, an image tag or a prefetch. - Frappe also applies its CSRF-token check to POST requests, so cross-site forgery is harder as well. - Read-only endpoints can say so explicitly. For example, `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py:388` uses `methods=["GET"]`. The decorator also appears on class methods, for example on `Customer` in `customer.py` (line 206) and on `Issue` in `issue.py` (line 120). These are document methods and use the same decorator syntax. **Concrete endpoints with `methods=["POST"]`** - `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py` has the most. These endpoints all create or reconcile documents: - `update_bank_transaction` - `create_journal_entry_bts` - `create_payment_entry_bts` - `create_bulk_internal_transfer` - `create_internal_transfer` - `create_bulk_bank_entry_and_reconcile` - `create_bank_entry_and_reconcile` - `create_bulk_payment_entry_and_reconcile` - `create_payment_entry_and_reconcile` - `reconcile_vouchers` - `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`: `make_quality_inspections` - `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py`: `update_company_master_and_address` - `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/lead.py`: `add_lead_to_prospect` - `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/mapper.py`: `make_lead_from_communication` - `erpnext/accounts/bulk_payment.py`, `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py`, `erpnext/setup/doctype/employee/employee.py`, `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/batch/batch.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/warehouse/warehouse.py`, `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py`, `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py`, `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/opportunity.py`, and `erpnext/support/doctype/issue/issue.py`: each has at least one POST-only endpoint. I did not look up their function names. My grep output was cut off at 40 matches, so this list is not complete. Other whitelisted endpoints in the repo may use the same restriction.

I did not read Frappe's own source, so the enforcement behaviour below is how I understand Frappe to work, not something I checked in this repo. **Mechanism** State-changing endpoints are declared as `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` instead of plain `@frappe.whitelist()`. Frappe records the allowed HTTP verbs for each whitelisted function. When a request arrives at `/api/method/<dotted.path>`, the request handler checks the verb against that list. A GET to a POST-only function is rejected with a `PermissionError` (HTTP 403 or 405). That blocks CSRF-style attacks, prefetching and link-triggered writes, because a GET can no longer create, save or submit documents. Plain `@frappe.whitelist()` lets any verb through, so only the endpoints that carry `methods=["POST"]` are restricted. On the client side, the caller uses `type: "POST"`. final answer
**How the progress is computed** The logic is in `RequiredItemsService` in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`. `WorkOrder.refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing` and `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items` in `work_order.py` delegate to it. 1. `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items` runs when a transfer Stock Entry is submitted or cancelled. - It calls `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)`. That query sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` per item. The grouping is by `item_code` and `original_item`, so substitute items count toward the item they replace. - It writes each total to the matching `required_items` row as `transferred_qty`. - It then calls `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing`. - `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing` runs only the recompute step. It is used for status decisions and doesn't touch the per-row quantities or stock reservations. 2. `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing` sets `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` in one of three ways: - **Job Card transfers:** if the work order has operations and `transfer_material_against == "Job Card"`, it returns early. Job Card logic handles that case. - **Entries with `fg_completed_qty`:** if `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty("Material Transfer for Manufacture", ...)` returns a non-zero sum of `fg_completed_qty`, that sum is used. This is the direct-transfer and excess-transfer path. - **Pick list flow:** pick lists set `fg_completed_qty = 0`, so the sum above is zero. The code then works out, for each required item, the fraction `transferred / required_qty`. It takes the minimum fraction across all items and caps it at 1.0. The result is `min_fraction * work_order.qty`. - Items with `include_item_in_manufacturing` unset, or a required quantity of 0 or less, are skipped. - A partial pick that covers only some items therefore can't mark the work order as fully transferred. The slowest item sets the progress. **What prevents over-transfer** These checks are in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py`. - **`_validate_no_excess_transfer`** - It runs in `validate_component_and_quantities` when `fg_completed_qty` is 0 and the entry has a work order. That is the pick list case. - For each item it computes pending as `required_qty - transferred_qty` from the work order's `required_items`. It sums the `qty` of the entry's rows that have a source warehouse. - If a total exceeds pending, it throws "Excess Material Transfer. Maximum transferable quantity is …". - It is skipped for returns. It is also skipped when Manufacturing Settings `backflush_raw_materials_based_on` is "Material Transferred for Manufacture". - **`get_pending_raw_materials`**, via `_is_overproduction_allowed` and `_calculate_item_transfer_qty` - These cap the auto-filled quantity at `required_qty - transferred_qty`. - Overproduction is allowed only up to the limit `qty * (1 + pct/100)`. The percentage is Manufacturing Settings `transfer_extra_materials_percentage`, or `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order` if that is unset. - If everything is already transferred, the user sees "All items have already been transferred for this Work Order." - **`WorkOrder.validate_qty`** in `work_order.py` (around line 869) covers work order quantity validation. I didn't read it, so I can't confirm what it checks.

It does nothing if `skip_transfer` is set. - It calls `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)`. That sums `transfer_qty` from the Stock Entry Detail rows of the work order's Material Transfer for Manufacture entries. It groups by `item_code` and `original_item`, so a substitute item's transfer is credited to the item it replaced. - It writes each total to the matching required-items row with `row.db_set("transferred_qty", ...)`. - It then calls `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing`. - `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing` runs only the recompute step. It is used to get a status decision from fresh data. 2. `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing(transferred_items)` sets `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` and has three cases: - If the work order has operations and `transfer_material_against == "Job Card"`, it returns without changing the field. In that case the Job Card sets it through `JobCard.set_transferred_qty` and `set_transferred_qty_in_work_order`, using the minimum completed quantity across operations. - If the sum of `fg_completed_qty` over the transfer entries is non-zero, it uses that sum. This is what happens for direct stock entries and for excess transfers. It reads the sum through `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty`. - Pick lists set `fg_completed_qty` to 0, so for partial pick-list transfers the sum is 0 and it falls through to the third case. For each required item it computes `transferred / required_qty`. It takes the smallest of those fractions, caps it at 1.0, and sets the field to `min_fraction × work_order.qty`. The most under-supplied item sets the progress, so partial batches don't mark the work order as fully transferred too early. **What prevents over-transfer** - **Planned-quantity cap.** `StatusService.update_work_order_qty` (in `work_order/services/status.py`) calls `_update_qty_for_purpose` for each purpose, including Material Transfer for Manufacture. That function checks that the transferred quantity is not above `qty + allowance% × qty`. If it is, it throws `StockOverProductionError` ("cannot be greater than planned quantity"). `_qty_allowance` takes the percentage from `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order` in Manufacturing Settings. If that is 0, it uses `transfer_extra_materials_percentage` for transfers. `_skip_transfer_purpose` skips this check when transfers are tracked against a Job Card. - **Additional transferred quantity.** If `additional_transferred_qty` is set, `WorkOrder.validate_additional_transferred_qty` (in `work_order.py`) throws unless `material_transferred_for_manufacturing + additional_transferred_qty` is within `qty` plus the `transfer_extra_materials_percentage` from Manufacturing Settings. - **Stock entry validation.** `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py` throws "Row {0}: Transferred quantity cannot be greater than the requested quantity." **How the progress is computed** The main code is `RequiredItemsService` in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`. `StatusService` in `.../work_order/services/status.py` also takes part. The `WorkOrder` methods in `work_order.py` only delegate to these services. 1. `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items()` runs when stock entries change. It calls `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)`. That query sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` over submitted "Material Transfer for Manufacture" entries for the work order. `_material_transfer_filter` applies those conditions. Rows are grouped by `(item_code, original_item)`, so substitute items count toward the item they replace. 2. The same method writes each total into the matching required-item row with `row.db_set("transferred_qty", …)`. It then calls `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()`. 3. `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` sets `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` in one of three ways: - **Job Card transfers:** if `transfer_material_against == "Job Card"` and the work order has operations, it returns early. `job_card.py` (around line 1271) sets the field from the minimum completed quantity across operations. - **Direct stock entries:** if `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty("Material Transfer for Manufacture", …)` returns a non-zero sum, the field is that `SUM(fg_completed_qty)`. This keeps excess-transfer tracking correct. - **Pick-list partial transfers:** pick-list entries have `fg_completed_qty = 0`, so the sum is zero and a min-fraction calculation is used instead. For each required item that is included in manufacturing, it computes `transferred / required`. It takes the minimum across items and caps it at 1.0. The result is `min_fraction * work_order.qty`. A work order is therefore only as "transferred" as its scarcest raw material, and partial batches don't mark it complete early. 4. `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` does the same recompute without touching the per-row quantities or stock reservations. `StatusService` calls it (status.py around line 94) before deciding between "Not Started" and "In Process". With min-fraction progress at 0, an item that has been partly transferred can still push the work order to "In Process". **What prevents over-transfer** - **Remaining quantity per item:** in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py`, `_calculate_item_transfer_qty()` computes `pending_to_issue = required_qty - transferred_qty`. The row's `transferred_qty` is the one kept up to date by the service above. It also computes `desire_to_transfer = fg_completed_qty * required_qty / max_qty`. `_resolve_transfer_qty()` then limits the quantity to the pending amount unless `can_transfer` is true. `can_transfer` is true when the desired quantity fits within the pending quantity, when backflush is based on "Material Transferred for Manufacture", or when overproduction is allowed. If nothing is left to transfer, the user sees the message "All items have already been transferred for this Work Order." - **Overall limit:** `_is_overproduction_allowed(max_qty)` in the same file compares `material_transferred_for_manufacturing + fg_completed_qty` against `max_qty` plus a tolerance. The tolerance is `transfer_extra_materials_percentage` or `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order` from Manufacturing Settings. - **Pick-list filters:** `pick_list.py` (around line 1350) and `stock_reservation_entry.py` (around line 1575) only consider work orders where `qty > material_transferred_for_manufacturing`. A fully transferred work order stops being offered for further pick-list transfers. - **Job Card flow:** `job_card.py` (around line 1233) throws "Cannot transfer more than Required Qty". I did not trace the full stock-entry validation path. There may be further checks in `stock_entry.py`, such as `validate_work_order_status`, that I didn't read.

When raw materials reach a Work Order in partial batches, the progress figure comes from item-level quantities, and the cap on over-transfer is a tolerance check against the planned quantity. I read the code but did not run it. I did not trace how the Stock Entry or Pick List side calls into these functions, so I can't say which hooks trigger them. ## How progress is computed The logic lives in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`, in `RequiredItemsService`. `WorkOrder` in `work_order.py` only delegates to it. 1. **Entry points.** `StatusService.update_status` in `services/status.py` calls `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` first. That is so pick-list-driven transfers show up in the status decision straight away. It then calls `update_required_items()`, which runs `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items()`. Both end in `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing(transferred_items)`. 2. **Per-item totals.** `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)` sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` over the submitted transfer entries. It groups by `(item_code, original_item)`, so a substitute item is credited to the item it replaced. `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items` writes these sums to each required-item row's `transferred_qty`. 3. **Recompute.** `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing` sets `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` in three steps: - It returns early if the Work Order transfers against Job Cards, because that case uses the minimum completed quantity across operations. - If `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty("Material Transfer for Manufacture", ...)` returns a non-zero value, it uses that. This is the sum of `fg_completed_qty` over submitted Stock Entries, and it is the direct-transfer and excess-transfer path. - Otherwise, which is the pick-list case because those entries have `fg_completed_qty = 0`, it uses the minimum fraction across items. For each included required item it computes `transferred / required_qty`, takes the minimum, caps it at 1.0, and multiplies by `Work Order.qty`. Because of the minimum, a partially fulfilled pick list doesn't mark the Work Order as fully transferred until every raw material has been transferred in full. If item A is 100% transferred and item B is 40%, progress is 40% of the Work Order quantity. 4. **Status.** `_submitted_status` and `_has_transferred_material` use this value to decide between "Not Started" and "In Process". ## What prevents over-transfer - **Per-purpose cap.** `StatusService.update_work_order_qty` loops over `_QTY_PURPOSES` and calls `_update_qty_for_purpose`. That function recomputes the quantity for the purpose. If it exceeds `qty + allowance% × qty`, it raises `StockOverProductionError` ("cannot be greater than planned quantity"). `_qty_allowance` takes the allowance from Manufacturing Settings. It uses `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order`, and for transfers it falls back to `transfer_extra_materials_percentage`. `_skip_transfer_purpose` skips the check for Job Card transfers. - **Additional transfers.** If `additional_transferred_qty` is set, `WorkOrder.validate_additional_transferred_qty` in `work_order.py` runs. It requires `material_transferred_for_manufacturing + additional_transferred_qty` to stay within `qty × (1 + transfer_extra_materials_percentage/100)`. Otherwise it throws and tells the user to raise the percentage in Manufacturing Settings. - **Fraction cap.** In the pick-list path, `min(min_fraction, 1.0)` stops the recorded progress from exceeding the Work Order quantity. This caps the recorded figure; it doesn't block the transfer itself.

That sums `transfer_qty` per item from submitted "Material Transfer for Manufacture" entries. It groups by `item_code` and `original_item`, so substitute items are credited to the item they replace. The result is stored in each required-item row's `transferred_qty`. - It then calls `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing`. That method works out, for each required item, the fraction `transferred / required_qty`. It takes the minimum fraction across all items and caps it at 1.0. final answer
When raw materials reach a Work Order in partial batches, ERPNext recomputes "material transferred for manufacturing" from the item-level quantities actually moved. Several guards then stop it from over-transferring. I read the code paths below but didn't run any of this. **How progress is computed** All of this is in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`, in `RequiredItemsService`. - `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items()` runs after a stock entry is submitted or cancelled. - It calls `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)`. That sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` per item. It groups by `item_code` and `original_item`, so a substitute item's transfer counts toward the item it replaced. - It writes each total to the matching `required_items` row's `transferred_qty`. - It then calls `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()`. - `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` does only the recompute step. `StatusService` (`work_order/services/status.py`) calls it before choosing between Not Started and In Process. - `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` handles three cases: 1. **Job Card transfers.** If the order has operations and `transfer_material_against == "Job Card"`, it returns without changing anything. The job card sets the value separately (`job_card.py`, around line 1271) as the minimum completed quantity across operations. 2. **Stock entries with `fg_completed_qty` set.** If the sum of `fg_completed_qty` over "Material Transfer for Manufacture" entries is non-zero, that sum is used. `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty` computes it. 3. **Pick-list transfers.** These set `fg_completed_qty = 0`, so the code takes the minimum fraction across required items. For each included item with a positive `required_qty`, it divides the transferred quantity by the required quantity. It caps the smallest of those fractions at 1.0 and multiplies by `work_order.qty`. The result is saved with `db_set`. Because the minimum fraction is used, a partially fulfilled pick list can't mark the order as fully transferred. One short item holds the whole figure down. **What prevents over-transfer** - **When the stock entry is built:** - `get_pending_raw_materials()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py` caps each item at what is still pending. `_calculate_item_transfer_qty()` computes the pending amount as `required_qty − transferred_qty`. - The amount the user wants to transfer is `fg_completed_qty × required_qty / wo.qty`. - A transfer beyond the pending amount is allowed only if `_is_overproduction_allowed()` returns true, or the backflush setting is "Material Transferred for Manufacture". - `_is_overproduction_allowed()` compares the already-transferred figure plus `fg_completed_qty` against `qty` plus the larger-priority percentage. It uses `transfer_extra_materials_percentage` if set, otherwise `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order`, both from Manufacturing Settings. - `_resolve_transfer_qty` returns the final quantity. If nothing is left, the code shows "All items have already been transferred for this Work Order." - **After the transfer is posted:** `StatusService.update_work_order_qty()` in `work_order/services/status.py` calls `WorkOrder.validate_additional_transferred_qty()` in `work_order.py` when `additional_transferred_qty` is set. - It allows `qty × (1 + transfer_extra_materials_percentage / 100)`. - It throws if `material_transferred_for_manufacturing + additional_transferred_qty` exceeds that limit. - **Pick list side:** `pick_list.py` (around line 1350) only picks for work orders where `wo.qty > wo.material_transferred_for_manufacturing`, so a fully transferred order is excluded.

final answer
`make_gl_entries(gl_map, cancel=False, adv_adj=False, merge_entries=True, update_outstanding="Yes", from_repost=False)` is the single entry point for posting or reversing GL Entries. It lives in `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`. I read the file and grepped for callers, but I didn't trace every call site's arguments. ## What it does today If `gl_map` is empty, nothing happens. **Posting path (`cancel=False`)**, in this order: 1. **Budget validation.** `BudgetValidation(gl_map).validate()` runs unless "use legacy budget controller" is set in Accounts Settings. It is skipped for Period Closing Voucher. 2. **`make_acc_dimensions_offsetting_entry`.** For accounting dimensions that have an offsetting account and auto-balancing enabled, it appends mirror entries. These apply only when the dimension has more than one value across the entries. It mutates `gl_map` in place. 3. **Validations.** `validate_accounting_period` and `validate_disabled_accounts` run here. 4. **`process_gl_map(gl_map, merge_entries, from_repost)`:** - `distribute_gl_based_on_cost_center_allocation` splits entries by Cost Center Allocation. It is skipped for Period Closing Voucher. - If `merge_entries` is true, `merge_similar_entries` runs. - `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative` always runs. 5. **Saving.** If more than one entry remains: - `create_payment_ledger_entry` runs, except for Period Closing Voucher. It receives `adv_adj`, `update_outstanding` and `from_repost`. - `save_entries` runs. If exactly one entry remains, it throws "Incorrect number of General Ledger Entries found". **Cancel path (`cancel=True`)** calls `make_reverse_gl_entries(gl_map, adv_adj, update_outstanding)`. None of the validation, merge or round-off steps run. ## Merging and deduplication - **`merge_similar_entries`** skips any entry with `_skip_merge`. - **Merge key.** `get_merge_properties` and `get_merge_key` build the key from account, cost_center, party, party_type, voucher_detail_no, against_voucher, against_voucher_type, project, finance_book, voucher_no, advance_voucher_type and advance_voucher_no. Every accounting dimension is added to the key. - **Summing.** `check_if_in_list` finds the first entry with the same key. The code sums debit, credit, and the account-currency and transaction-currency variants of each into that entry. - **Zero filter.** After merging, entries with zero debit and zero credit (at company precision) are dropped. The exception is a Journal Entry whose type is "Exchange Gain Or Loss". - **Negative amounts.** `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative` moves negative amounts to the opposite side. If `post_net_value` is set, it also nets debit against credit. - **`merge_entries=False`.** Only the merge step is skipped. The cost-center distribution and the negative toggle still run. ## Validation and round-off in `save_entries` - `validate_cwip_accounts` runs unless `from_repost` is set. - `process_debit_credit_difference` rounds each entry to company precision and sums debit minus credit. - The allowance is `5/10^precision` for Journal Entry and Payment Entry, and 0.5 for everything else. - A difference above the allowance raises "Debit and Credit not equal". Exchange Gain Or Loss Journal Entries are exempt. - A difference of at least one unit of precision but within the allowance calls `make_round_off_gle`. The difference is recomputed afterwards and checked again. - `make_round_off_gle` picks the account as follows: - It uses the company's "Round Off for Opening" account if any entry has `is_opening == "Yes"`, and throws if that is unset. Otherwise it uses the company's Round Off Account, falling back to the default expense account. - If an entry for that account already exists (outside Period Closing Voucher), it is adjusted. It is removed if the residual is below one unit of precision. - The cost center is the voucher's own `cost_center` if it has one, otherwise the company's Round Off Cost Center. Missing settings throw. - The entry carries debit, credit and transaction-currency amounts, with party and against-voucher fields cleared. `update_accounting_dimensions` fills in the dimensions. - `check_freezing_date` and `validate_against_pcv` run. The second is skipped for Period Closing Voucher. - For each entry, `validate_allowed_dimensions` runs, then `make_entry` creates and submits a GL Entry. The GL Entry carries the `from_repost`, `adv_adj` and `update_outstanding` flags. - After submit, `validate_expense_against_budget` runs unless the posting is a repost or a Period Closing Voucher. It also runs on cancellation, but only for Journal Entry. ## What a change would affect **Direct callers of the function** - `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`: `StockController.make_gl_entries` calls it with `from_repost`. This covers Stock Entry, Stock Reconciliation, Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Subcontracting Receipt and Landed Cost Voucher. Purchase Receipt and Delivery Note appear in the stock-doctype call list; Stock Entry, Stock Reconciliation and Subcontracting Receipt appear there too. - Sales Invoice (`sales_invoice.py`, around line 1045). - Purchase Invoice (`purchase_invoice.py`, around line 678, with the GL composer in `services/gl_composer.py`). - Payment Entry (`payment_entry.py`, lines 1298 and 1316). It passes `cancel`, `adv_adj`, `merge_entries` and `update_outstanding`. - Journal Entry (`journal_entry.py`, around line 878). - Invoice Discounting (`invoice_discounting.py`, line 190). It passes `update_outstanding="No"`. - Period Closing Voucher (`period_closing_voucher.py`, line 475) and Process Period Closing Voucher (`process_period_closing_voucher.py`, line 438). Both pass `merge_entries=False`. - Deferred accounting: `accounts/deferred_revenue.py` (line 580, a wrapper that passes `merge_entries=True`) and Process Deferred Accounting (`process_deferred_accounting.py`, line 54, which passes `cancel=1`). - Assets: Asset (`asset.py`, line 981), Asset Capitalization (`asset_capitalization.py`, line 390, with `merge_entries=False`) and Asset Repair (`asset_repair.py`, line 315, which passes `cancel` positionally). **Indirect callers, which depend on each document's `make_gl_entries` wrapper** - `accounts/utils.py`, around line 1705, calls `voucher_obj.make_gl_entries(gl_entries=expected_gle, from_repost=True)`. - `repost_accounting_ledger.py` calls the wrappers with several different signatures. It uses `inspect.getfullargspec` to check for a `cancel` argument. - `controllers/ledger_preview.py` calls `doc.make_gl_entries()` for the GL preview. - Landed Cost Voucher and the Asset mapper (`assets/doctype/asset/mapper.py`, which calls `journal_entry.make_gl_entries(1)`). - Patches: v13_0 `modify_invalid_gain_loss_gl_entries`, v12_0 `repost_stock_ledger_entries_for_target_warehouse` and v15_0 `repost_gl_entries_with_no_account_subcontracting`. **Related code to review** - The functions that `make_gl_entries` calls (`process_gl_map`, `merge_similar_entries`, `save_entries` and `make_round_off_gle`) are used elsewhere too. - `make_reverse_gl_entries` is called directly by Sales Invoice, Asset Capitalization and Stock Controller. ## Risks - Several callers pass `cancel` positionally, for example `make_gl_entries(gl_entries, cancel)`. Reordering or removing parameters would break them silently. - Changing the merge key or the zero-entry filter changes the shape of the posted GL Entries. The Exchange Gain Or Loss exception, the `_skip_merge` flag, the dimension handling and Period Closing Voucher's `merge_entries=False` all depend on it. - Round-off behavior is tied to the per-voucher-type allowance, to `is_opening`, and to the Period Closing Voucher exceptions. - Reposting compares or regenerates GL Entries, so a merge change can show up as repost differences. The existing GL tests should catch this: Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry, stock vouchers and Period Closing Voucher.

`make_gl_entries(gl_map, cancel=False, adv_adj=False, merge_entries=True, update_outstanding="Yes", from_repost=False)` is at `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py:34-74`. Everything below comes from reading that file and grepping for callers. I did not trace call chains deeper than one hop. ## What it does today If `gl_map` is empty, it does nothing. **Posting (`cancel=False`), in order:** 1. **Budget validation.** This runs only if `use_legacy_budget_controller` is off and the voucher type is not "Period Closing Voucher". It calls `BudgetValidation(gl_map).validate()`. 2. **Accounting dimension offsets.** `make_acc_dimensions_offsetting_entry` appends offsetting rows to `gl_map` in place. It does this for dimensions that have an offsetting account configured and take more than one value in the map. 3. **Validations.** - `validate_accounting_period` - `validate_disabled_accounts` (from `services/gl_validator.py`) 4. **`process_gl_map(gl_map, merge_entries, from_repost)`:** - **Cost center allocation.** `distribute_gl_based_on_cost_center_allocation` runs for every voucher type except Period Closing Voucher. It splits a row across sub cost centers by percentage and validates the budget against the main cost center unless `from_repost`. Round-off account rows are moved to the first allocated cost center instead of being split. - **Merging.** If `merge_entries` is true, `merge_similar_entries` runs. - **Sign normalisation.** `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative` always runs. It flips negative debits or credits to the other side, and nets debit against credit when `post_net_value` is set. 5. **Row-count check and saving:** - **More than one row:** - For anything except a Period Closing Voucher, it calls `create_payment_ledger_entry` in `accounts/utils.py`, passing `adv_adj`, `update_outstanding` and `from_repost`. - It then calls `save_entries`. - **Exactly one row left after processing:** it throws "Incorrect number of General Ledger Entries found…". **Cancelling (`cancel=True`):** it calls `make_reverse_gl_entries(gl_map, adv_adj, update_outstanding)`. There is no validation, merging or round-off on this path. ## Merging and deduplication `merge_similar_entries` builds a merge key for each row (`get_merge_key`, `get_merge_properties`). The key fields are: - `account`, `cost_center`, `party`, `party_type` - `voucher_detail_no`, `against_voucher`, `against_voucher_type` - `project`, `finance_book`, `voucher_no` - `advance_voucher_type`, `advance_voucher_no` - every accounting dimension - **Skipped rows:** rows with `_skip_merge` set are kept as they are. - **Summing:** rows with the same key have their debit and credit summed. That covers the base, account-currency and transaction-currency fields. - **Zero-amount rows:** rows where debit and credit are both zero at GL Entry precision are dropped. The exception is a Journal Entry whose `voucher_type` is "Exchange Gain Or Loss". ## Round-off handling This happens inside `save_entries`, through `process_debit_credit_difference`. It is not in `make_gl_entries` itself. - **Order in `save_entries`:** 1. `validate_cwip_accounts`, unless `from_repost`. 2. `process_debit_credit_difference`. 3. `check_freezing_date`. 4. `validate_against_pcv`, except for Period Closing Vouchers. 5. For each row, `validate_allowed_dimensions` and then `make_entry`, which creates and submits a GL Entry and runs `validate_expense_against_budget` when it applies. - **Rounding:** `get_debit_credit_difference` rounds each row's debit and credit to the GL Entry precision and sums the difference. It does the same for the transaction-currency fields. - **Allowance:** the tolerated difference is `5 / 10**precision` for Journal Entry and Payment Entry, and 0.5 for every other voucher type. - **Difference above the allowance:** it throws "Debit and Credit not equal…". Journal Entries of type "Exchange Gain Or Loss" are exempt. - **Difference of at least one precision unit but within the allowance:** `make_round_off_gle` runs. - It uses the company's round-off account. If any row has `is_opening` set to "Yes", it uses the "Round Off for Opening" account instead, and throws if that account isn't set. - It reuses an existing round-off row if there is one, or appends a new one. - An existing round-off row is removed if the remaining difference is below one precision unit. - The row gets the round-off cost center, accounting dimensions via `update_accounting_dimensions`, and no party or against-voucher fields. - **Final check:** the difference is recomputed and must be within the allowance, or it throws again. ## What a change would affect **Direct callers of the module-level function** (the graph shows four callers, and grep found more): - **Accounting:** - `accounts/doctype/repost_accounting_ledger/repost_accounting_ledger.py::start_repost` - `accounts/doctype/process_period_closing_voucher/process_period_closing_voucher.py::summarize_and_post_ledger_entries` (`merge_entries=False`) - `accounts/utils.py::repost_gle_for_stock_vouchers` - `controllers/ledger_preview.py::get_accounting_ledger_preview` - **Invoices and payments:** - Sales Invoice (around line 1045) - Purchase Invoice (around line 678) - Payment Entry (lines 1298 and 1316, using `cancel`, `adv_adj`, `merge_entries` and `update_outstanding`) - Journal Entry (around line 878) - **Other accounting documents:** - Invoice Discounting (`update_outstanding="No"`) - Period Closing Voucher (`merge_entries=False`) - Process Deferred Accounting (`cancel=1`, keyword `gl_map=`) - `accounts/deferred_revenue.py` (lines 444 and 580) - **Assets:** - Asset (around line 981) - Asset Repair (around line 315) - Asset Capitalization (`merge_entries=False, from_repost=…`) - **Stock:** `controllers/stock_controller.py` (around line 205, `from_repost`). This is the shared path for Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry, Stock Reconciliation, Subcontracting Receipt and Landed Cost Voucher. **Indirect callers.** Many doctypes expose their own `make_gl_entries` method (for example Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry and `StockController`). These call the shared function on submit and cancel, so they inherit any change. Reposting code calls those methods rather than the shared function: - `repost_accounting_ledger.py` calls them at lines 192–213, including with `from_repost=True`. - `accounts/utils.py:1705` passes `gl_entries=expected_gle, from_repost=True`. - `landed_cost_voucher.py` passes `via_landed_cost_voucher=True`. - Several patches under `erpnext/patches/v12_0`, `v13_0` and `v15_0` call the doctype methods too. **Risks to check before changing it:** - **Positional arguments:** some callers pass arguments positionally, such as `make_gl_entries(gl_entries, cancel)` in Asset Repair. Others use a keyword like `gl_map=`. Changing parameter order or names breaks them silently or loudly. - **Merge key and `_skip_merge`:** changing them alters ledger granularity. This affects payment ledger entries, outstanding calculations, and the reposting comparison in `repost_gle_for_stock_vouchers`, which compares expected against existing GL entries. - **Merge and `from_repost`:** `merge_entries` and `from_repost` flow into `process_gl_map`, cost center allocation and budget validation. Changing the merge behaviour also changes `create_payment_ledger_entry`, because it runs on the merged rows. - **Round-off:** it runs after merging, so it depends on the merged rows. The Period Closing Voucher and Exchange Gain/Loss special cases are scattered across several functions, and each would need the same update. - **Tests:** any tests under `erpnext/accounts` that assert GL entry counts or merged rows would be affected. I did not search the tests.

`make_gl_entries(gl_map, cancel=False, adv_adj=False, merge_entries=True, update_outstanding="Yes", from_repost=False)` is the entry point for posting a voucher's GL map. It lives in `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`. I read that file in full. I only counted the callers by grep and did not open each one. ## What it does today **Empty map:** if `gl_map` is empty, it does nothing. **Cancel path (`cancel=True`):** it skips everything below and calls `make_reverse_gl_entries(gl_map, adv_adj, update_outstanding)`. **Posting path (`cancel=False`):** 1. **Budget check.** Unless Accounts Settings has `use_legacy_budget_controller` set, or the voucher is a Period Closing Voucher, it runs `BudgetValidation(gl_map).validate()`. 2. **Dimension offsetting.** `make_acc_dimensions_offsetting_entry` adds offsetting entries for accounting dimensions. 3. **Pre-merge validations.** `validate_accounting_period` and `validate_disabled_accounts`. 4. **Processing.** `process_gl_map(gl_map, merge_entries, from_repost)` does three things: - **Cost center allocation:** `distribute_gl_based_on_cost_center_allocation` splits entries across cost centers (skipped for Period Closing Voucher). - **Merge and dedup:** if `merge_entries` is true, `merge_similar_entries` runs. Entries marked `_skip_merge` are left alone. - The merge key is built by `get_merge_properties` and `get_merge_key`. It covers account, cost_center, party, party_type, voucher_detail_no, against_voucher, against_voucher_type, project, finance_book, voucher_no, advance_voucher_type, advance_voucher_no, plus every accounting dimension. - Entries with the same key are summed in `debit`, `credit`, and their account-currency and transaction-currency variants. - Entries whose debit and credit are both zero at company-currency precision are dropped. The exception is a Journal Entry of type "Exchange Gain Or Loss". - **Sign normalisation:** `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative` moves negative debits into credits and negative credits into debits. It also nets debit against credit when `post_net_value` is set. 5. **Entry-count check.** If more than one entry remains, it continues. If exactly one remains, it throws "Incorrect number of General Ledger Entries found…". If none remain, it does nothing. 6. **Payment ledger.** For anything other than a Period Closing Voucher, it calls `create_payment_ledger_entry`. 7. **Saving.** `save_entries` runs `validate_cwip_accounts` (not on repost) and `process_debit_credit_difference`. It then runs `check_freezing_date` and `validate_against_pcv` (not for Period Closing Voucher), then `validate_allowed_dimensions` on each entry. Finally `make_entry` creates and submits each GL Entry document, then calls `validate_expense_against_budget` unless it is a repost or a Period Closing Voucher. That budget check also runs on cancelled Journal Entry entries. **Round-off handling** is in `process_debit_credit_difference`. - It rounds debit and credit to the GL Entry precision and computes the difference in company currency and in transaction currency. - The allowance is `5 / 10**precision` for Journal Entry and Payment Entry, and 0.5 for everything else. - If the difference exceeds the allowance, it throws "Debit and Credit not equal". The exception is a Journal Entry of type "Exchange Gain Or Loss". - If the difference is within the allowance but at least one unit of precision, `make_round_off_gle` appends or adjusts a round-off GL Entry: - It uses the company's round-off account and cost center, or the "Round Off for Opening" account when any entry has `is_opening == "Yes"`. It throws if that account is not set. - If a round-off entry already exists and the remaining difference is below one unit of precision, it removes that entry instead. - It clears party and against-voucher fields on the round-off entry and applies accounting dimensions. - It then rechecks the difference against the allowance and throws again if it is still too large. ## What the change would affect A grep for `make_gl_entries` outside test files found 79 occurrences in 27 files. Many of these are the per-doctype methods of the same name (for example `SalesInvoice.make_gl_entries`), which are wrappers around the general_ledger function. I did not confirm which are direct calls to the general_ledger function and which are only the wrappers' own definitions and callers. - **Accounts doctypes** - Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry. - Period Closing Voucher and Process Period Closing Voucher. - Invoice Discounting. - Process Deferred Accounting, plus `accounts/deferred_revenue.py`. - Repost Accounting Ledger, which has 8 occurrences and passes `from_repost`. - `accounts/utils.py`. - **Stock and controllers** - `controllers/stock_controller.py`, which is the base for Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry, Stock Reconciliation and Subcontracting Receipt. - Those five doctypes each reference it directly. - Landed Cost Voucher. - `controllers/ledger_preview.py`, which builds a GL preview. - **Assets** - Asset, `asset/mapper.py`, Asset Repair, Asset Capitalization. - **Patches** - `v13_0/modify_invalid_gain_loss_gl_entries.py`. - `v15_0/repost_gl_entries_with_no_account_subcontracting.py`. - `v12_0/repost_stock_ledger_entries_for_target_warehouse.py`. - **Tests and other apps** call it too. I did not check them, but any positional arguments or `merge_entries` behaviour they rely on would also break. ## Risks to check before changing it - **Signature:** callers pass `cancel`, `adv_adj`, `merge_entries`, `update_outstanding` and `from_repost`, some positionally and some by keyword. Search for each of those before reordering or renaming anything. - **Merge behaviour:** changing the merge key or the zero-entry filter changes which GL Entries get created. That affects the payment ledger, because `create_payment_ledger_entry` runs after merging. It also affects the Exchange Gain Or Loss special case and the round-off entry logic. - **Period Closing Voucher:** it skips budget validation, cost center distribution and the payment ledger. Keep those branches intact. - **Reposts:** `from_repost` skips CWIP validation and budget validation. Repost Accounting Ledger depends on this.

The rest depends on `cancel`. **Posting (`cancel=False`):** 1. **Budget check.** Unless the legacy budget controller is on or the voucher is a Period Closing Voucher, it runs `BudgetValidation(gl_map).validate()`. 2. **Dimension offsets.** `make_acc_dimensions_offsetting_entry` appends balancing entries to the offsetting account. It also computes the transaction-currency difference. - **Allowance.** Journal Entry and Payment Entry get an allowance of `5 / 10**precision`. A Period Closing Voucher skips this existing-entry search. - **Final check.** The difference is recomputed and the same allowance check runs again. ## What a signature or merge change would touch **Inside the module:** - `process_gl_map` is also called from other places, so changes to its merge arguments also reach those callers. - `merge_similar_entries`, `get_merge_properties`, `get_merge_key` and `check_if_in_list` are used by the merge path. - `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative` is also used by `repost_gle_for_stock_vouchers` in `erpnext/accounts/utils.py`. - `process_debit_credit_difference` is also called from `erpnext/accounts/utils.py`. **Controllers:** - **Shared dispatch.** Many documents define their own `make_gl_entries` method. All the Trends reports share it. The Group By branch is `if filters.get("group_by")`, and it runs three queries: 1. **Based-on rows (`data1`).** This query groups by `conditions["group_by"]`. Each row is added to the output with a blank cell inserted at the group-by column index (`ind`). 2. **Distinct group values (`row`).** For each based-on row, a `SELECT DISTINCT(sel_col)` finds the group values (item, customer or supplier). It filters on `based_on_key = data1[d][0]`. 3. **Per-group detail (`row1`).** This runs for each distinct value in `row`. It sums the period-wise columns for that group value and based-on key. The code never reaches `row1[0][0]` or `row1[0][j]`, so there is no `IndexError`. The based-on parent row and the other group values still appear, and the report finishes normally. The total row is built afterwards from `data1` by `calculate_total_row`. If `row1` has data, the code builds a row `des`, one blank cell per column. It sets `des[ind] = row[i][0]` (the group value) and `des[ind-1] = row1[0][0]` (the currency). It then copies the period values from `row1[0][j]` into `des[j + inc]`. The offset `inc` is 3 for Customer or Supplier based-on, 2 for Item, and 1 otherwise. This guard is a recent addition. The `based_on_key` variable, taken from the first column of `conditions["group_by"]`, is the key the detail queries match against. Without the guard, an empty `row1` would have raised an index error.
